artigo.texto: More than 50 people marched to Ameren Missouri’s St. Louis headquarters Saturday to speak out against the company’s newly published plans to build more fossil fuel resources in the coming 20 years. The group wore nature-inspired costumes while holding signs calling for clean energy. The People’s Joy Parade and the Sierra Club organized the demonstration with speakers from Tenants Transforming St. Louis, the Missouri Coalition for the Environment and Labadie Environmental Organization. “We can create the clean energy future that we need. We can create it through people power, through love of our communities, and through good organizing,” said Jenn DeRose, the Sierra Club’s campaign organizing strategist for Beyond Coal in Missouri. She stressed the need to develop energy sources like solar and wind power with battery storage to make it available around the clock. Ameren Missouri recently released a new long-range plan that would significantly increase the amount of power plants in its portfolio to meet growing demand for electricity. The company said that growth is primarily driven by new large data centers moving to Missouri. The new resource plan increases the number of new natural gas power plants to nine while also extending the lives of two existing coal plants. Both resources emit planet-warming gases that contribute to climate change. Patricia Schuba lives near the Labadie Coal Plant, which will now operate all four of its units until 2042, rather than shuttering two units in 2036. The plant is about 35 miles west of St. Louis on the Missouri River. Schuba and other demonstrators hit a Labadie power plant piñata that was filled with candy made to look like coal. She said she is not normally that kind of person but feels “righteous rage” about the plans to keep the plant that she said has made her and her neighbors sick open longer. “We approached the solution in a peaceful way, but we need to express that we are very angry with these decisions,” Schuba said. “The people sitting in the building behind me make those decisions every day for all of us, for our children, for future generations, and we need to hold them accountable.” Ameren Missouri executive Ajay Arora told St. Louis Public Radio in September that keeping Labadie operating longer would save customers money. “Labadie remains one of the most affordable plants in the country and recognizing the economic conditions for all our customers and how important reliability and affordability is, that's really factored into delaying the retirement of a few of the Labadie units by a few years,” Arora said. On Saturday, the protesters said electricity is not affordable in the St. Louis region and condemned Ameren’s practice of disconnecting customers who are behind on their bills. “They say they care about affordability and that they're here to serve us. Is that true?” Sarah Watkins, an organizer with Tenants Transforming St. Louis, asked the crowd. “If Ameren cares so much about us, then why are tens of thousands of families losing their electricity every year?” Bills could rise again soon as Ameren is asking Missouri regulators to approve a rate increase for customers. Both the proposed rate increase and the new integrated resource plan are subject to approval by Missouri’s Public Service Commission.

"Os ataques em Kiev atingiram o centro de dados do Ukrsibbank, utilizado pelas Forças Armadas da Ucrânia para coletar, processar e armazenar informações de inteligência", afirmou o ministério. A pasta russa também relatou um ataque a um navio de carga seca no mar Negro que transportava suprimentos militares para o porto de Odessa. Os ataques ocorrem após uma série de investidas russas contra a infraestrutura de dados da Ucrânia no último mês, incluindo instalações operadas pela Ukrtelecom, DreamLine, Omega Telecom, Kyivstar, Vodafone e Datagroup em Kiev. Tais instalações, segundo relatos, forneciam serviços de inteligência, comunicações e armazenamento de dados às forças ucranianas. artigo.texto: Why Choose TOPCon 3.0 Solar Modules? Vertex N G3 is built on Trinasolar's TOPCon 3.0 cell technology and incorporates four core technological upgrades. Ultra cell platform technology increases power output and bifacial performance. Multi-cut technology and edge passivation technology reduce current losses and improve shading and hot-spot performance. Ultra-high density packaging technology improves module efficiency and energy yield. A bifaciality of 85% ± 5% supports additional rear-side generation where site conditions allow, while the −0.26%/°C power temperature coefficient helps limit power losses in Vietnam's hot climate. A maximum annual degradation of 0.35% from the second year onward, backed by a 30-year power warranty, provides developers with a defined basis for modelling long-term output and project revenue. Solar and Battery Storage Applications in Vietnam Trina Storage also presented Elementa 3, its 6.25MWh utility-scale BESS built on in-house 587Ah cells. Elementa 3 supports renewable energy integration and flexible power supply, including in grid-connected projects, as Vietnam expands solar generation to meet growing demand from industry and AIDCs. Trinasolar's solar-plus-storage project at Corona Resort in Phú Quốc provides a local proof point of its PV and BESS delivery capabilities. The project combines a 3MWp solar installation with a 10MWh AC-coupled BESS retrofit, demonstrating how battery storage can be added to an existing commercial solar system. Vertex N G3 and Elementa 3 extend Trina's portfolio with higher module output and greater storage capacity per container, giving developers and EPC contractors greater flexibility in meeting project capacity and site requirements.

artigo.texto: Michael Burry adds BYD shares after calling automaker a potential low-cost leader Michael Burry, the investor known for predicting the 2008 housing-market crash, added shares of Chinese electric-vehicle maker BYD Company BYDDY BYDDF in a portfolio reshuffle disclosed in early October. The purchase was reported in an October 6 portfolio update on Burry’s Substack. The update also included changes to his positions in JD.com JD and several other stocks. The number of BYD BYDDF shares purchased and the size of the position were not disclosed. Burry’s earlier analysis outlined the investment case for BYD BYDDF, highlighting its valuation, manufacturing scale and technology. He wrote, “I would be an aggressive buyer at HK$75 or better, if the thesis still holds at that time.” He also highlighted BYD’s BYDDF cost advantages from controlling more of its supply chain. “BYD is potentially the lowest-cost producer of vehicles in the world thanks to its vertically integrated model at scale,” he wrote. Battery technology is another part of the investment thesis. BYD’s in-house Blade battery uses lithium iron phosphate chemistry. Burry’s analysis highlighted the chemistry’s cost and safety advantages over nickel-manganese-cobalt batteries, while acknowledging its lower energy density. He also pointed to international expansion as a potential source of operating leverage. “I believe BYD is an exceptionally well-run and technologically advanced company today, and I believe long-term ROIC will settle above 10%,” Burry wrote. In his March analysis, Burry also compared BYD BYDDF with Tesla TSLA, noting that BYD generated more revenue despite having a much smaller market capitalization. The comparison underscored his view that investors valued the two businesses differently. Burry had indicated in September that he was monitoring BYD BYDDF. Asked about the stock, he said, “Yes, I am watching it,” after previously disclosing that he did not own shares. artigo.texto: Redata torna Brasil mais competitivo para atrair data centers, diz diretor da Brasscom Sergio Sgobbi afirma que a aprovação do PLP contribui para a previsibilidade regulatória e tributária que influencia o ritmo do mercado Em setembro, o Plenário do Senado aprovou o projeto que institui o Redata, Regime Especial de Tributação para Serviços de Data Center, que prevê a suspensão de tributos federais para empresas do setor que cumpram critérios ambientais, sociais e econômicos estipulados pelo governo. Dois dias depois da aprovação, Câmara e Senado aprovaram o Projeto de Lei Complementar, que flexibiliza regras fiscais para viabilizar a concessão dos incentivos previstos no regime. Os dois textos ainda precisam da sanção presidencial para entrar em vigor, enquanto seguem aguardados pelas empresas e entidades do segmento. Isso porque, com a sua aprovação, as regras de atuação do setor, nas esferas jurídicas, competitivas e tributárias, ficarão mais claras, o que deve refletir em mais segurança e tranquilidade para quem quer operar no País. Para Sergio Sgobbi, Diretor de Relações Institucionais e Governamentais da Associação das Empresas de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação e de Tecnologias Digitais do Brasil (Brasscom), a aprovação torna o Brasil mais atrativo para investidores e empresas do setor, especialmente em tempos de um ambiente global altamente competitivo. “O Redata contribui justamente para aumentar a competitividade nesse processo”, afirma. Confira, a seguir, a entrevista completa. Engrenagens do Crescimento — Depois de quase um ano de tramitação, com a medida provisória caducando e o projeto de lei parado no Senado, qual foi o momento mais crítico para a aprovação do Redata na avaliação da Brasscom? Sergio Sgobbi — O momento mais crítico ocorreu justamente quando houve a caducidade da medida provisória sem a conversão imediata em lei, ampliando a incerteza regulatória em torno do tema. Para um setor intensivo em capital e com ciclos longos de investimento, a previsibilidade é um elemento importante na tomada de decisão. O principal risco naquele momento era o adiamento de projetos e a perda de competitividade do Brasil frente a outros mercados que também disputam investimentos em infraestrutura digital. Alguns investimentos foram para outras geografias, mas o Congresso Nacional, a tempo, tomou a decisão correta pela aprovação do PL. Engrenagens do Crescimento — A Brasscom, junto com outras entidades, pediu ajustes no Projeto de Lei Complementar (PLP) para viabilizar os incentivos ainda em 2026. Pode explicar qual foi o ajuste e dizer o que estava em jogo se essa costura não tivesse funcionado? Sergio Sgobbi — O objetivo do ajuste foi garantir a previsão de renúncia fiscal para que os incentivos pudessem produzir efeitos ainda em 2026, compatibilizando o regime com as regras fiscais vigentes. Sem a solução legislativa, não haveria como o presidente sancionar a lei, ou seja, o PLP aprovado deu contornos legais ao orçamento da União para que a política pública do Redata possa acontecer em 2026. Engrenagens do Crescimento — Na votação da Câmara, o Redata quase ficou de fora do relatório do PLP e só voltou por emenda de plenário. Como o setor reagiu a esse momento de incerteza e o que isso revela sobre a prioridade que o tema tem no Congresso? Sergio Sgobbi — O setor acompanhou com atenção esse processo e intensificou o diálogo institucional para demonstrar a relevância estratégica do estabelecimento dessa política pública. O episódio mostrou que existe reconhecimento crescente da importância do tema, mas também evidencia que a agenda ainda precisa disputar espaço com outras prioridades legislativas. A aprovação posterior demonstrou a capacidade de articulação entre governo, Congresso e setor produtivo em torno de uma agenda considerada estratégica para o País. Engrenagens do Crescimento — O texto final trocou a exigência de energia limpa por baixa emissão, permitindo que gás natural e fontes nucleares supram data centers, além das fontes eólica e solar. Como a Brasscom avalia essa mudança — foi decisiva para destravar investimentos represados? Sergio Sgobbi — A Brasscom entende que o mais importante é garantir uma expansão sustentável da infraestrutura digital, conciliando segurança energética, competitividade e compromisso ambiental. A adoção do conceito de fontes renováveis ou de baixa emissão amplia as opções tecnológicas disponíveis e oferece maior flexibilidade para o desenvolvimento dos projetos, sem afastar os objetivos de sustentabilidade previstos no regime. Engrenagens do Crescimento — Que tipos de empresas associadas à Brasscom estavam com decisões de investimento “em compasso de espera” à espera do Redata e quais eram os negócios estimados? Qual é a expectativa de quando esses projetos devem sair do papel? Sergio Sgobbi — A Brasscom não trabalha com uma estimativa consolidada de investimentos efetivamente represados. O que observamos é que operadores de data centers, provedores de infraestrutura digital, empresas de nuvem e investidores analisam continuamente diferentes mercados para alocação de capital. Em um ambiente global altamente competitivo, a previsibilidade regulatória e tributária influencia o ritmo de tomada de decisão. artigo.texto: BYD's September Deliveries Hit 463,561 as Battery Expansion Takes Priority Over US Entry Published on 10/12/2026 at 06:01 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD shares closed Friday at EUR 8.65, up 4.2%, lifted by a broad rebound across Chinese auto and EV counters rather than any single company announcement. Market chatter attributed the sector-wide bounce to a technical recovery following several sessions of declines, with worries over peak-season demand and China-EU trade friction already largely reflected in prices. Despite the day's advance, the stock remains down 19% year-to-date. Exports do the heavy lifting The operational picture offers firmer ground. Worldwide vehicle deliveries reached 463,561 units in September, a 17.0% year-on-year increase and a fresh high for 2026. With domestic Chinese demand subdued, overseas shipments carried the load: exports of passenger cars and pickups totaled 180,700 units, up 153.9% from a year earlier. That export momentum has become the primary driver of overall volume even as conditions at home stay demanding. Institutional analysts took note. On October 8, SDIC Securities International reiterated its buy rating on BYD with a target price of HKD 103.6, citing the roughly 464,000 vehicles delivered in September. A day later, UOB Kay Hian kept BYD as a preferred pick. The brokerage trimmed its broader auto-sector sales forecasts for 2026 through 2028 after a weaker-than-expected first nine months, but flagged that rising international trade barriers could, over the long run, favor established leaders like BYD over smaller rivals. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Battery capacity and new models in the spotlight Alongside the market recovery, BYD is pressing ahead on the operational front. The company reports sustained strong demand for its fast-charging models and has made expanding production capacity for the second generation of its in-house Blade battery its top priority, aiming to secure delivery capability over the long term. The model lineup at home is widening too. Pre-orders have opened for the second-generation Seagull, with an official launch slated for the fourth quarter; pricing has not yet been disclosed. On the commercial side, BYD reached 150,000 units of alternatively powered commercial vehicles built, as a fully electric Q3 tractor unit rolled off the line at its Huai'an plant. Washington stays off the map Geographic expansion, by contrast, is proceeding selectively. Executive Vice President Stella Li, speaking to Reuters on October 8, described the geopolitical situation as the single biggest challenge to further growth. For that reason, BYD will hold off on launching passenger cars in the United States for now, citing a lack of the necessary stability and clarity in that market. Exports to other regions have been unaffected. Ad BYD Stock: New Analysis - 12 October Fresh BYD information released. What's the impact for investors? Our latest independent report examines recent figures and market trends.

artigo.texto: DE SOTO, Kan. — KSHB 41 reporter Isabella Ledonne reports on stories in Overland Park, Johnson County and topics about government accountability. Share your story idea with Isabella. — The company behind one of the hyperscale data center proposal projects in De Soto, Kansas, announced it is preparing to provide direct credits of up to $1,000 for every household in the city. Digital Realty is preparing its 300-acre site for a data center at Astra Enterprise Park near the Panasonic Plant. Construction is expected to start in 2027. Beale Infrastructure has started construction on its data center campus down the road from Panasonic and Digital Realty's site. But even with the promise of Digital Realty's money, neighbors are still skeptical of what the project could mean for their everyday life. "Is that enough?" neighbor Sara VanDeCreek said. "How much is the value of our community?" Digital Realty reached out to me on Friday to announce the company is planning to give every household a yearly credit up to $1,000 for the next 10 years to be used for property tax and/or utility relief. —Watch: De Soto data center plans to offer $1,000 to households; neighbors skeptical— It's among the first in the Kansas City metro to offer an incentive directly to residents. "De Soto has a lot of people that could use $1,000 a year," VanDeCreek said. But to some neighbors, that check could mean something else. "It's a bribe, is what it looks like," neighbor Toni Caldwell said. "If you can't give us the true answers, then don't come to me with money and expect me to believe what's going on or accept that money." Both Caldwell and VanDeCreek have been outspoken against De Soto's two data center developments, even helping launch a petition earlier this month to block the development. They explained that petition has gained more than 400 signatures. Digital Realty's announcement to invest $20 million in a community fund in the form of direct relief for residents has been met with some skepticism. "They're not really answering the questions that we have," VanDeCreek said. "I don't think it sweetens the deal and I think it's purposeful that it's coming out right now before they ask for tax incentives to help with bonds." I asked Digital Realty why the company is offering this and if it's meant to offset any anticipated rise in residential electric and water bills with the operation of the data center. "This commitment is designed to deliver tangible benefits for De Soto residents while we invest for the long term," a spokesperson said over email. "It accelerates benefits the community will receive and is a reflection of our broader approach to responsible development, collaboration and being a good neighbor in our project communities." "A community partner first of all is transparent," VanDeCreek said. Neighbors are still wanting answers to their biggest concern: the long-term impacts of having data centers in the community. It's a question residents say they haven't gotten the answer to with either data center proposal. "A good community partner is one you can trust," Caldwell said. "I don't trust either one of them right now." Digital Realty did not make anyone available for an on-camera interview. "This community investment accompanies Digital Realty's entire development in De Soto and reflects our long-term commitment to local partnerships," a spokesperson wrote in a statement. "We look forward to continuing this investment in the community as the project moves forward." The company is expected to have a TIF district public hearing at the city council meeting on Nov. 19. The City of De Soto is helping Digital Realty with the distribution and plans for the direct relief payments, though no funds are expected to come out of the city's general revenue fund. “De Soto and the developers of Astra Enterprise Park have spent decades planning for the future of this historic site, with the City focused on ensuring its redevelopment creates tangible benefits and improves quality of life for our residents,” De Soto mayor Rick Walker said. “Digital Realty’s commitment builds on that vision in a meaningful way by investing directly in the people who call De Soto home.” —

artigo.texto: Two Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) in East Hampton Town will continue to suspend operation until a controversial fire suppression agent is removed from the facilities, announced Suffolk County Executive Ed Romaine on Oct. 9. The move comes after the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation issued a report in early September concluding that the chemical in the fire suppression system, NOVEC 1230, was the likely cause of contamination of nearby public drinking water wells after a May 2023 fire at the BESS at Cove Hollow Road in East Hampton. Both the Cove Hollow Road BESS and another BESS near Fort Pond in Montauk are operated by NextEra Energy and National Grid, and both will be shut down until the chemical is removed, town and county officials announced this week. Two Suffolk County Water Authority wells were taken offline after the chemicals were discovered earlier this year, and the Water Authority sued NextEra and National Grid in June, alleging that more than 2.2 million gallons of fire suppression water containing the chemicals could have run off the site in the 30 hours the fire suppression system was running during the fire. This summer, East Hampton made a series of demands for safer operations at the Cove Hollow BESS, including new engineering controls capable of containing all fire water and runoff, a revised emergency and safety plan, complete and certified technical information, a hazardous-waste management plan and an independent study of whether the facility remains necessary for the East End electric grid. On Sept. 29, after the DEC released its findings the East Hampton Town Board unanimously authorized litigation against the companies. Within 24 hours of authorization of the litigation, Town Supervisor Kathee Burke-Gonzalez announced that both facilities had temporarily shut down operations, until Oct. 9. “This is the action we demanded, and I am pleased that NextEra responded swiftly to my Sept. 29 letter and the Town Board’s action,” said Ms. Burke-Gonzalez in a statement Oct. 3. “The Board has authorized litigation, retained counsel and taken the steps necessary to go to court to secure this shutdown.” “The town retains all of its legal rights should NextEra fail to follow through on removing all NOVEC 1230 from both facilities and ensuring appropriate fire safety and environmental measures are in place.” On Oct. 9, County Executive Ed Romaine a new extension of the shutdown that “will remain in place until these changes are put into effect,” referring to the removal of the NOVEC 1230 fire suppression chemicals. He said the extended suspension followed “weeks of discussions between Suffolk County and NextEra.” Mr. Romaine said in his announcement that both he and East Hampton Village Mayor Jerry Larsen sent letters to the chief executives of NextEra Energy and National Grid urging them to suspend operations at the East Hampton facility until the investigation is completed. There’s currently an effort afoot for a write-in campaign for Mr. Larsen against Ms. Burke-Gonzalez in this November’s election, after Mr. Larsen failed to win a primary against the sitting supervisor this June. “NextEra continues to negotiate in good faith and address the concerns of the residents,” said Mr. Romaine. “As we await remediation plans to be approved by the NYS Department of Environmental Conservation, we must all work together to ensure the best interests of the residents surrounding these facilities.” The DEC announced Sept. 10 that its field investigation of the contaminated drinking water suggests that the perfluorinated compound in the water “may be linked to the use of a vapor-based waterless fire suppression system” that, when combined with water, can break down into the chemical compound now found in public drinking water wells. The primary compound found in initial testing is known as perfluoropropanoic acid (PFPrA), which is known by chemists as an ultra-short chain PFAS. The agency says its final reporting later this fall and other site related documents will be made available here: https://extapps.dec.ny.gov/data/DecDocs/2601953/. Mr. Romaine said Suffolk County has also drilled monitoring wells to investigate the contamination and supports the Water Authority’s litigation against NextEra. Anyone interested in more information can contact the Suffolk County Department of Health at 631.852.6700. artigo.texto: - Energy - 2 min read India's battery energy storage sector set for 91% growth to 302GWh by FY32E: Nuvama Cumulative BESS capacity could rise to 302 GWh from 6.3 GWh, driven by renewable integration and falling costs, creating growth opportunities for domestic manufacturers. India's Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sector is projected to register a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 91 per cent between FY26 and FY32E, according to a recent report by Nuvama. The expansion reflects a critical infrastructure cycle designed to support renewable integration, grid balancing, and round-the-clock power requirements across the country. The report noted that cumulative capacity will surge from 6.3 GWh to 302GWh over the same period, with annual additions climbing from 5.7GWh in FY26 to 56 GWh by FY32E. The report noted that the Central Electricity Authority (CEA) estimates national BESS demand at 236 GWh by FY32 and 1,840 GWh by 2047. "We estimate annual BESS additions to rise from 5.7 GWh in FY26 to 56 GWh by FY32E, taking cumulative capacity from 6.3GWh to 302GWh (91 per cent CAGR) over FY2632E," the report said. "With 89 per cent of current requirements met through imports, falling battery costs, alongside a likely ALMM-like framework, could accelerate adoption, localisation and domestic capacity growth. Although Li-ion occupies 98 per cent of the BESS market, sodium-ion technology and China+1 themes are an opportunity for India," the report added. Manufacturing economics reveal distinct margins across end-markets, with commercial, industrial, and retail segments yielding spreads of $18 to 23 per kilowatt-hour, corresponding to EBITDA margins of 17 to 20 per cent. By contrast, the utility segment records spreads of $8 per kilowatt-hour and an EBITDA margin of 9 per cent. "Our analysis shows attractive cell-to-pack manufacturing economics with materially differentiated spreads across end-markets," the report noted. "Even with low spreads of USD8/kWh (EBITDA margin 9 per cent) for the Utility segment, our calculation and channel checks indicate a one-to-two-year payback." The report also highlighted that while returns for an integrated BESS facility yield a modest internal rate of return of 12 per cent, domestic production maintains a distinct cost advantage through capital expenditure of $80 million per gigawatt-hour, coupled with production-linked incentive support of ₹181 billion for 50 GWh and competitive labour expenses. Cell-to-pack configurations demonstrate an internal rate of return of 31 per cent. "We believe with policy support, localisation and scale, integrated BESS could open up export-led growth," the report noted. Financially, BESS integration is estimated to contribute 17 to 60 per cent to company revenues by FY28. Premier presents an opportunity of ₹103 billion, representing 60 per cent of its projected FY28 revenue, while Vikram is positioned for a 54 per cent revenue uplift. "Despite early battery ambitions and potential BESS addition of 17-60 per cent to FY28E revenue, most listed solar/BESS players' earnings are yet to capture meaningful BESS contribution," the report stated. "At 17x FY27E EPS, solar/BESS trades at a 77 per cent discount to battery chemicals and a 64 per cent discount to battery IPP peers. As capacity ramps up, we believe BESS could emerge as a strong driver of earnings upgrade and valuation re-rating," the report said.

artigo.texto: Harrisburg, Pa. — The president of Concerned Citizens of Montour County was among the speakers at a state Capitol rally on Oct. 6, where organizers say more than 250 people from across Pa. called on Gov. Josh Shapiro and legislators to impose a moratorium on data center development. “All they have to fight with is money,” said Sam Burleigh, president and co-founder of the Montour County group. “We have collective voices, elective powers, constitutional laws, and home field advantage. Together we can beat them! Unite and fight!” Burleigh has also previously spoken at meetings focused on Muncy and Gregg townships' proposed data centers. The rally in the Capitol Rotunda was organized by the Better Path Coalition, No False Climate Solutions PA, and 30 partner organizations. Speakers addressed concerns including surveillance, affordability, impacts on health, the environment, and agriculture, threats from artificial intelligence to intellectual property, and the future being left to children. Speakers during the event criticized legislators for what participants described as “putting polluters before people via data center deals that were brokered outside of the public’s view.” The rally closed with speeches on what organizers called the state government’s failure to enforce Pa.’s Green Amendment, Article 1, Section 27 of the state constitution. “Once again, our elected officials are leaping before they look to do the bidding of an industry,” said Karen Feridun, co-founder of the Better Path Coalition and No False Climate Solutions PA and the rally’s emcee. “Governor Shapiro claims to have changed his position on data centers, but his recent Executive Order implementing his GRID initiative is all about making sure data centers are built, not taking the break the public is demanding to decide what role, if any, hyperscale data centers and generative AI should play in Pennsylvania.” Stuart Day of Ohio Valley Allies, who described himself as a Pa. farmer and investigative journalist, compared the expansion of hyperscale data centers to the shale-gas boom. “I believe AI and the infrastructure supporting it represent a transformative moment in human history — and decisions of that magnitude demand deliberation, transparency, and meaningful public participation. This development should not be foisted upon communities and landowners without independent economic and environmental analysis, strong oversight, enforceable protections, and an honest accounting of who receives the benefits and who carries the costs. Rural Pennsylvania has heard promises of salvation from outside industries before; we should have learned by now that something this consequential demands caution, wisdom, and a process with real teeth,” Day said. Hilary Flint, program director at Center for Organizing, said more than 40,000 people have joined the Pennsylvania Data Center Resistance Facebook group. “People understand that projects of this scale will shape their communities for decades, and they are saying no. This movement is growing, it is organized, and we will keep showing up because communities deserve more than a seat at the table. They deserve the power to say no to what gets built in their own backyards,” Flint said. The rally also launched a fall campaign of letters from specific groups of residents explaining why signers oppose data center development. The letters will be delivered to Gov. Shapiro, state legislators, and the winners of the upcoming election. Josephine Gingerich, health advocacy outreach coordinator at Physicians for Social Responsibility PA, led a delegation to Gov. Shapiro’s office to deliver a letter from 80 health professionals. Letters from faith leaders, artists and other creatives, and parents and guardians are open for signatures at bit.ly/NoDataCentersPA, with letters from other groups being planned. Maya van Rossum, founder of Green Amendments For The Generations and the Delaware Riverkeeper, said residents “have a true and enforceable right to pure water, clean air, and healthy environments” under the state constitution. “We are offended when our governor, legislators, or local officials throw out our environmental rights — the rights specifically respected in our state constitution’s declaration of rights — as a throwaway talking point. Our environmental rights are clear and enforceable here in Pennsylvania. When our governor, legislators, or local officials try to ignore or evade them, we will stand up and defend them.” Other speakers listed by organizers included representatives of the Phoenixville Liberation Center, March on Harrisburg, the Delaware Riverkeeper Network, Make the Road PA, Chester Residents Concerned for Quality Living, and the Intertwined faith community.

artigo.texto: This electric vehicle company has fallen sharply from its all-time high as competition, weak financial performance, and continued cash burn weighed on the stock. The company is now focusing on improving volumes, expanding its product portfolio and scaling battery manufacturing to support its turnaround. With a market capitalisation of Rs. 16,254 cr, the shares of Ola Electric Mobility Ltd closed at Rs. 35.12 per share, up from its previous close of Rs. 34.50 per share. The stock made a high of Rs. 158 per share in Aug 2024, trading at a discount of 78% from that level. The stock has gone through a major de-rating Ola Electric’s sharp correction from its all-time high reflects a significant reset in investor expectations. Investors initially valued the company on the assumption that it could rapidly scale its electric two-wheeler business and establish a strong leadership position in India’s EV market. However, weaker-than-expected volumes, persistent losses, cash burn, and rising competition have led to a substantial stock de-rating. Also Read: Empower India Shares Jump 30% in 5 Trading Sessions: Here’s What’s Driving the Rally The company’s financial performance has also remained under pressure. While Ola has started showing some sequential improvement in deliveries, the recovery has not yet translated into meaningful revenue growth or profitability. This has made investors increasingly focused on whether the company can build a sustainable business model rather than simply increase sales volumes. Deliveries have improved, but revenue remains under pressure Deliveries nearly doubled quarter-on-quarter to approximately 39,200 units, while orders rose to around 44,000 units. The improvement suggests that the company’s recent product launches, pricing initiatives and efforts to strengthen its distribution network are beginning to support volumes. However, revenue remained a major concern. Q1FY27 revenue declined 45% year-on-year to Rs. 455 crore, highlighting the impact of lower realisations and the company’s earlier weakness in volumes. At the same time, the net loss narrowed to Rs. 336 crore from Rs. 500 crore in Q4FY26. Although the sequential improvement is encouraging, the company still needs a sustained improvement in revenue, gross margins and operating profitability before the turnaround can be considered established. Competition has intensified sharply Ola’s biggest challenge is no longer simply expanding the electric two-wheeler market, but defending its position within it. Established manufacturers such as TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto, along with EV-focused players such as Ather Energy, have strengthened their presence in the segment. The competitive pressure has affected Ola’s market share and forced the company to rethink its sales strategy. It is expanding its product portfolio, increasing distribution and moving toward a larger network of dealer-operated outlets. The objective is to improve customer reach while reducing the cost and capital intensity associated with an entirely company-operated retail network. The key question for investors is whether Ola can sustain its recent improvement in deliveries while rebuilding its market position without relying excessively on discounts or sacrificing margins. New products could help Ola regain volumes Product launches remain central to Ola’s recovery strategy. The company has been expanding beyond its premium positioning and targeting a broader customer base with products such as the S1Z. A wider product portfolio could allow Ola to address different price segments and increase its addressable market. Technology is another important part of the strategy. Ola is increasingly focusing on its own battery technology and has been integrating its Bharat Cell LFP technology into its products. The company has also received BIS certification for its 46100 LFP cell, which is an important step toward commercialising its indigenous battery technology. If these products achieve better cost efficiency, reliability and scale, they could help Ola improve competitiveness while reducing dependence on externally sourced battery technology. Battery manufacturing could become a long-term differentiator Ola’s battery strategy is potentially one of the most important parts of its long-term business model. The company is expanding its Gigafactory and moving toward greater vertical integration, with the objective of manufacturing critical battery components in-house. The company has also secured the full five-year Advanced Chemistry Cell Production Linked Incentive window through CY2031, potentially making it eligible for incentives of up to Rs. 7,240 crore. This could significantly support the economics of its battery manufacturing operations if Ola can achieve the required production scale and manufacturing yields. However, battery manufacturing also brings execution risks. The company must demonstrate that it can achieve consistent yields, scale production efficiently, and commercialise its cells at competitive costs. Therefore, the Gigafactory could become either a major competitive advantage or an additional source of capital expenditure and cash burn, depending on execution. Fresh capital provides additional financial flexibility Ola has continued to raise capital to support its operations and growth plans. The company recently approved a Rs. 1,000 crore rights issue, following the Rs. 780 crore QIP completed in June. The proposed use of the rights proceeds provides some indication of management’s priorities. The company plans to use around Rs. 350 crore for debt repayment, while proposing approximately Rs. 400 crore for organic growth. Founder and CEO Bhavish Aggarwal also said he will subscribe to his entitlement. The fundraising provides Ola with additional liquidity at a time when the business is still loss-making. artigo.texto: A expansão de setores de alta tecnologia pode não produzir oportunidades de trabalho na mesma proporção dos investimentos anunciados na Tailândia. O alerta é de Tanit Sorat, vice-presidente da Confederação de Empregadores do Comércio e da Indústria da Tailândia. Segundo ele, data centers são altamente automatizados, empregam poucos especialistas em tecnologia da informação e, em muitos casos, recorrem a profissionais estrangeiros. Esses empreendimentos também demandam grandes volumes de eletricidade e água para refrigeração. No primeiro semestre de 2026, os pedidos de investimento cresceram 73% em um ano, para 1,47 trilhão de bahts, distribuídos por 1.299 projetos. O setor digital respondeu por 1,12 trilhão de bahts, impulsionado por inteligência artificial e data centers. Principais fatos e números - Pedidos de investimento somaram 1,47 trilhão de bahts no primeiro semestre de 2026. - O valor representou crescimento anual de 73%, segundo o Conselho de Investimento da Tailândia. - Foram registrados 1.299 projetos no período. - O setor digital respondeu por 1,12 trilhão de bahts. - Até 75% das peças, materiais e equipamentos para data centers precisam ser importados. - Data centers empregam poucos especialistas por serem altamente automatizados. Por que isso importa para empresários e investidores O volume de capital abre oportunidades para fornecedores de energia, refrigeração, infraestrutura digital e formação técnica. Entretanto, a elevada automação e a dependência de componentes importados limitam o efeito imediato sobre empregos e indústria local. Empresas também devem considerar a pressão de longo prazo sobre eletricidade e água, além da possível necessidade de contratar especialistas estrangeiros. Os dados disponíveis mostram forte intenção de investimento, mas não informam quanto será efetivamente executado, quantos postos serão criados nem em que prazo. Essa incerteza exige cautela ao projetar demanda, capacidade produtiva e retorno econômico.

artigo.texto: Transnordestina, data centers e atração de novas empresas serão as prioridades econômicas do novo mandato do governador reeleito do Ceará, Elmano de Freitas (PT), que inicia em 2027. Siga o canal de Economia no WhatsApp para ficar bem informado A informação foi dada em entrevista ao O POVO e à rádio O POVO CBN nesta sexta-feira, 9 de outubro. Sobre a Transnordestina, Elmano citou que a infraestrutura permitirá atrair investimentos para todo o Ceará, com foco principal no Interior. [SHORT_CODE_RECOMENDATION_HORIZONTAL_6ac943c3924a5] Nesse contexto, destacou que a ferrovia ajudará a transformar a região do Cariri, que engloba 29 municípios do Estado, em um grande polo logístico. Segundo ele, um dos desafios da gestão, no entanto, será descentralizar o desenvolvimento para as demais cidades da região. Elmano afirmou que pretende construir em Missão Velha (município distante 452,89 km de Fortaleza), na Região Metropolitana do Cariri, um porto seco para que o escoamento da produção possa ser realizado no local. Veja dicas rápidas sobre Educação Financeira no Dei Valor “É um desafio nosso porque temos Juazeiro, Crato e Barbalha crescendo. Precisamos pensar em outras cidades do Cariri para crescer de maneira aproximada, com Missão Velha, Campos Sales e outros municípios da microrregião do Cariri também se desenvolvendo”, comentou. O governador também anunciou a meta de integrar a Transnordestina à Ferrovia Norte-Sul, após a finalização das obras. A medida, para ele, permitirá ao Estado acessar a produção de grãos do Centro-Oeste do Brasil, já que a Norte-Sul interliga o Maranhão a São Paulo, passando por Tocantins, Goiás e Minas Gerais. “Nossa prioridade agora é vincularmos a Transnordestina à Ferrovia Norte-Sul, porque nós estaríamos trazendo para o Ceará toda a produção de grãos vindo lá do Centro-Oeste”, destacou. Acompanhe mais notícias de Economia no Linkedin do O POVO O gestor acrescentou que o agronegócio do País será impactado, pois os produtos passarão a contar com quatro portos para exportação: Itaqui (MA), Pecém (CE), Suape (PE) e Santos (SP), este último já integrado à malha ferroviária. O agronegócio também foi citado como prioridade. De acordo com Elmano, a gestão nos próximos quatro anos terá foco no fortalecimento do setor e na melhoria da qualidade de vida do trabalhador do campo. Outro ponto destacado foi o avanço tecnológico promovido pelos investimentos na construção de data centers no Estado. Segundo o governador, esses aportes favorecem o ambiente de negócios e a geração de empregos qualificados. Confira os assuntos econômicos no Ceará, no Brasil e no Mundo “Os data centers nos permitem vislumbrar uma ambiência para o desenvolvimento de empresas e a prestação de serviços nas áreas de tecnologia e segurança cibernética, além da formação de mão de obra para esse setor, garantindo empregos e salários melhores”, afirmou. No setor industrial, Elmano ressaltou que o Estado, a partir da Planta Automotiva do Ceará (Pace), localizada em Horizonte (a 42 km de Fortaleza), vem se consolidando como polo nacional e internacional de veículos elétricos. Ele revelou que há negociações em curso para a instalação de uma nova empresa no local, com anúncio previsto ainda para este ano. Detalhes sobre a companhia não foram divulgados devido a cláusulas de confidencialidade. [SHORT_CODE_RECOMENDATION_HORIZONTAL_6ac943c393da8] O governador relembrou as tratativas para atrair a produção de bobinas laminadas, classificada por ele como uma “indústria de base essencial para impulsionar outros setores produtivos”. “Queremos que o investimento possa iniciar o mais rápido possível”, pontuou. O planejamento estadual prevê ainda um impulso nos setores de mineração e gás natural, respaldado por convênios com a Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC) para estudos de viabilidade e confirmação de jazidas minerais. Elmano reforçou, por fim, a necessidade de ampliar os investimentos privados no Estado por meio de maior sinergia de planejamento entre o setor público e a iniciativa privada.

EDIÇÃO APRESENTADA POR: Brasil pode contar com 13 GW de flexibilidade no setor elétrico com baterias, reversíveis e resposta da demanda O Brasil pode ter mais de 13 gigawatts (GW) de flexibilidade operativa no setor elétrico até 2036 com o aumento da participação de baterias e usinas reversíveis e do uso do mecanismo de resposta da demanda, indica a consulta pública do Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia 2036 (PDE 2036), divulgado na quinta-feira (8/10). Veja o documento na íntegra em .pdf. Desse total, as baterias podem contribuir com 7,2 GW, aumento em relação aos 6,6 GW previstos no documento no ano anterior. - Os dois primeiros leilões de reserva de capacidade para a contratação de baterias, marcados para dezembro, serão um importante marco para a confirmação do espaço para esses projetos no Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN). Leia mais sobre isso em: Outra contribuição importante virá da resposta da demanda, modelo pelo qual grandes consumidores são remunerados para deslocar o horário de consumo. A contribuição prevista é de 4 GW, ante 3,2 GW no plano anterior. - Já as hidrelétricas reversíveis podem somar mais 2 GW, mas a viabilização desses recursos depende da capacidade dos arranjos de mercado e dos mecanismos de contratação de reconhecer adequadamente os diferentes atributos e serviços que podem ser prestados ao sistema por essas fontes, indica a EPE. São novos mercados que se ampliam num contexto de intensas mudanças no perfil da geração e do consumo no setor elétrico. O aumento da flexibilidade é importante para a operação do sistema elétrico diante do crescimento da demanda e da expansão da geração intermitente, sobretudo no modelo de micro e mini geração distribuída (MMGD). - Você viu aqui: - E aqui: O PDE prevê que o parque de geração brasileiro alcançará 382 GW em 2036, impulsionado principalmente pelo salto da MMGD para 92 GW. - Já o consumo de eletricidade será alavancado pelo aumento da eletromobilidade, pela atração de data centers e pela produção de hidrogênio renovável. A demanda vai crescer a uma taxa média de 3,4% ao ano até 2036, chegando a 979 TWh. - Os data centers trarão o aumento mais expressivo no consumo, com um crescimento de dez vezes na demanda, chegando a 30 TWh de eletricidade em 2036. - Mais detalhes em: Eletrificação cria nova corrida por energia no Brasil até 2036. - Vale a leitura: “Era da eletrificação” coloca redes sob pressão no mundo todo e demanda mudanças no planejamento, dizem executivos. Os fios soltos do setor elétrico. Armazenamento de energia, compensação pelo curtailment, leilões para contratação de reserva de capacidade e controle dos subsídios que pressionam a CDE podem parecer discussões distintas. Na prática, todas desembocam na mesma pergunta de sempre: quem deve pagar pelos custos necessários para manter o sistema equilibrado? Leia a análise de Gabriel Chiapinni Privatização da Petrobras. Nenhuma dessas empresas será tocada”, disse Sachsida em um vídeo publicado na rede social X na quinta-feira (8/10). Subvenções. artigo.texto: O olhar único que há 50 anos acompanha o que é notícia no Brasil e no mundo Diagnóstico sobre cadeia de minerais críticos e baterias no Brasil fica pronto no início de 2027 Um diagnóstico sobre minerais críticos, mapeando onde o Brasil já compete, onde a inserção é nascente e onde os desafios estruturais são mais profundos e identificando as reservas e a capacidade extrativa do país deve ficar pronto no início do ano que vem. O Brasil possui a segunda maior reserva de terras raras do mundo, com cerca de 21 milhões de toneladas, atrás apenas da China. O país, no entanto, responde por menos de 1% da produção global. O estudo inédito - voltado à cadeia de minerais críticos e baterias no Brasil - é o primeiro passo do acordo de cooperação técnica firmado entre a Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI), o Net Zero Industrial Policy Lab, da Universidade Johns Hopkins, e o Instituto E+ Transição Energética, para desenvolver estudos e propor políticas públicas relacionadas a minerais críticos. Um dos objetivos do estudo é apresentar recomendações ancoradas nas capacidades reais da indústria brasileira para extrair os minerais críticos e transformá-los em produtos, mirando as oportunidades concretas abertas pela transição energética e no contexto do programa Nova Indústria Brasil (NIB), afirma Fabrício Silveira, superintendente de Política Industrial da CNI. Os minerais críticos são estratégicos para a indústria. Com aplicação diretamente ligada à transição energética, digitalização, defesa e alta tecnologia. Tratam-se de recursos naturais amplamente utilizados em baterias, veículos elétricos, turbinas eólicas e painéis solares, entre outros produtos.

artigo.texto: Jeep Avenger X BYD Dolphin Mini: qual é o melhor carro por R$ 120 mil? Recém-chegado a combustão encarou o primeiro carro elétrico a figurar no top três dos mais vendidos do Brasil. A BYD prepara uma atualização de software para corrigir falhas de segurança identificadas na Shark 6, picape híbrida vendida na Austrália, essa é a nomenclatura utilizada fora do Brasil, mas trata-se da mesma picape vendida no país. Leia também O caso veio à tona após um experimento realizado por um especialista em cibersegurança, que conseguiu acessar funções do veículo e demonstrou como uma invasão poderia interferir na experiência do motorista. A investigação foi exibida pelo programa australiano Four Corners, da emissora ABC, em setembro. Durante o teste, o especialista Dan Hreszczuk conseguiu acessar o sistema de entretenimento, reproduzir áudios, visualizar imagens na central multimídia e travar as portas. Também foi possível acessar o microfone interno e acompanhar a localização do veículo. Leia também O episódio chamou atenção principalmente porque alguns desses recursos puderam ser acionados remotamente depois que o especialista instalou um aplicativo não autorizado no sistema do carro. A BYD investigou o caso e confirmou que identificou uma vulnerabilidade relacionada ao acesso a ferramentas de desenvolvimento do software da central multimídia. Como foi feita a invasão? Segundo a fabricante, o acesso à central ocorreu por meio de uma brecha relacionada ao Android Debug Bridge (ADB), ferramenta utilizada no desenvolvimento e na depuração de sistemas Android. Embora normalmente esteja desativada, uma falha permitiu habilitar esse recurso e instalar um aplicativo de terceiros sem confiança estabelecida. A BYD afirma que conseguiu reproduzir a vulnerabilidade em seus próprios testes. A empresa também esclareceu que, para acessar informações como a localização e o áudio captado pelo microfone, o procedimento exigia que o motorista autorizasse uma solicitação de permissão exibida na tela. Para corrigir o problema, a fabricante prepara uma atualização remota de software, que deverá eliminar o caminho utilizado para habilitar o ADB. Até o momento, não foi divulgada uma data para a liberação da correção. A empresa também avalia se vulnerabilidades semelhantes afetam outros modelos da marca. Faróis e limpadores também foram acionados O experimento foi além da central multimídia. Durante a demonstração, o especialista conseguiu acionar os limpadores de para-brisa e desligar os faróis enquanto a picape estava em movimento. Nesse caso, porém, o procedimento foi diferente. De acordo com a BYD e com o próprio pesquisador, foi necessário acessar fisicamente a fiação do veículo e conectar um dispositivo à rede interna de comunicação eletrônica, conhecida como CAN bus. Portanto, não se tratou de um comando executado simplesmente pela internet, sem contato com o carro. Leia também A fabricante informou que adotou novas medidas de proteção na interface de diagnóstico OBD, utilizada para acessar informações e sistemas eletrônicos do veículo. Entre as medidas estão o isolamento físico e a autenticação dos dispositivos conectados, com o objetivo de dificultar o acesso não autorizado a funções críticas. O especialista afirmou que não conseguiu acessar sistemas mais críticos, como os freios e as câmeras do veículo. Ainda assim, o teste mostrou que interferências em equipamentos como faróis e limpadores podem representar um risco à segurança, especialmente quando acontecem durante a condução. Limited (CATL) Largest global battery manufacturer by volume According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Advance Battery Technologies market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global market for Advance Battery Technologies is entering a phase of accelerated commercial scaling, driven by the limitations of conventional lithium-ion in safety, duration, and material criticality. This report analyzes the market for next-generation electrochemical energy storage beyond standard lithium-ion, including solid-state, advanced lithium variants, flow batteries, metal-air, and sodium-ion chemistries. The market is bifurcating into distinct technology pathways: solid-state and advanced lithium for high-energy-density mobility; flow and metal-air for long-duration stationary storage; and sodium-ion for cost-sensitive, high-safety applications. Commercial viability is shifting from cell-level $/kWh to total cost of ownership and levelized cost of storage, incorporating cycle life, safety systems, and balance-of-plant requirements. Supply chain bottlenecks have moved from raw material extraction to novel material synthesis and specialized manufacturing equipment, creating higher barriers than conventional gigafactory scaling. System integration complexity and multi-year qualification timelines are critical constraints, favoring players with deep testing resources and strategic partnerships. Procurement is moving from component-centric to performance-centric models, especially in stationary storage, where utilities and IPPs seek guaranteed performance. Geographic specialization is crystallizing, with IP and R&D in advanced economies, pilot-scale demonstration in regulatory-supportive markets, and GWh-scale output in regions with industrial policy. The forecast horizon 2026-2035 points to robust growth, with demand driven by grid modernization, renewable integration, and electrification of transport. The baseline scenario for the Advance Battery Technologies Market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 18.5%, reaching a market index of 545 by 2035 (2025=100). This outlook is supported by accelerating deployment of grid-scale energy storage, where flow and metal-air batteries are gaining traction for long-duration applications, and by the commercialization of solid-state batteries in premium electric vehicles. Demand-side indicators include utility procurement targets for storage capacity, renewable energy curtailment rates, and EV production volumes. The market is expected to bifurcate further, with sodium-ion capturing cost-sensitive segments and advanced lithium variants dominating high-performance mobility. Supply chain localization policies in North America and Europe will drive regional manufacturing capacity, while Asia-Pacific maintains leadership in cell production. Key risks include qualification delays, raw material price volatility, and competition from continued lithium-ion cost reductions. However, the fundamental drivers of safety, duration, and material diversity remain strong, positioning advanced battery technologies for sustained growth through 2035. The electric vehicle sector is the largest end-use for advanced battery technologies, driven by the need for higher energy density, faster charging, and improved safety. Currently, conventional lithium-ion dominates, but solid-state and advanced lithium variants are entering pilot production. Through 2035, as these technologies achieve commercial scale, they will enable longer range and shorter charging times, accelerating EV adoption. Demand-side indicators include EV sales volumes, battery pack energy density targets, and charging infrastructure build-out. The shift to solid-state will be gradual, starting with premium vehicles and expanding to mass-market models as costs decline. Key mechanisms include the replacement of liquid electrolytes with solid ones, enhancing safety and energy density, and the use of lithium-metal anodes. This transition will reduce reliance on graphite and cobalt, diversifying supply chains. Major automotive OEMs are investing heavily in solid-state battery development, often through partnerships with specialized firms. The sector's growth will be supported by government mandates phasing out internal combustion engines and consumer demand for better performance. Current trend: Rapid adoption of solid-state and advanced lithium batteries in premium and mid-range EVs. Major trends: Solid-state battery commercialization for premium EVs, Advanced lithium-ion with silicon anodes for increased energy density, Integration of battery management systems with fast-charging networks, Partnerships between automakers and battery developers, and Government incentives for EV adoption and local battery production. Representative participants: Tesla, Toyota, Volkswagen, QuantumScape, Solid Power, and SES AI. Stationary energy storage is the second-largest and fastest-growing end-use sector for advanced battery technologies, driven by the integration of renewable energy and grid modernization. Flow batteries, such as vanadium redox and zinc-bromine, are well-suited for long-duration applications (4+ hours) due to their scalability and long cycle life. Metal-air batteries, particularly iron-air, offer ultra-low-cost storage for multi-day applications. Currently, lithium-ion dominates short-duration storage, but flow and metal-air are gaining traction for longer durations. Through 2035, as renewable penetration increases, the need for long-duration storage will surge, supported by government auctions and utility procurement. artigo.texto: Um relatório global põe as baterias abaixo das turbinas a gás de pico no custo da energia. No Brasil, a corrida dos data centers por conexão já começou, e o primeiro leilão de baterias do país está marcado para 2 e 4 de dezembro. As baterias de quatro horas ficaram mais baratas que as turbinas a gás de ciclo aberto em todos os 43 mercados onde a Wood Mackenzie comparou as duas tecnologias. A conta é o custo nivelado da energia, o LCOE: o preço médio de cada megawatt-hora ao longo da vida da usina. O relatório saiu em outubro de 2026. “A mudança econômica é decisiva e está se ampliando”, disse Ahmed Jameel Abdullah, analista principal da Wood Mackenzie. Ele aponta dois motores. De um lado, faltam turbinas a gás e o combustível oscila. Do outro, a produção de baterias cresce. O que o estudo mede, e o que ele não mede A manchete que circulou fala em “data centers”, mas o relatório trata de custo de geração de pico, e não de um data center específico. A Wood Mackenzie compara uma bateria de quatro horas com uma turbina a gás de ciclo aberto. É o tipo de usina que as distribuidoras ligam só nas horas de maior consumo. - Energia renovável perde ritmo no Brasil com cortes de geração e incerteza para investidores - Áustria teve 43.300 tickets em 10 minutos para disputar R$ 215 milhões de subsídio solar que paga R$ 838 por kWp, enquanto no Brasil painel novo já paga 60% do Fio B - Usina solar de Indiana instalou 20 mil painéis por dia com 1.800 operários em 18 meses e está prestes a operar - Agricultor de Illinois tem 10 torres eólicas na fazenda e recebe cerca de R$ 600 mil por ano, mas no Nordeste os relatos vão de R$ 600 a R$ 2 mil por mês por torre A bateria não gera energia. Ela guarda a que veio do sol, do vento ou da rede e devolve na ponta. Por isso a conta fecha melhor onde a geração solar é barata para carregá-la. Segundo o mesmo relatório, a solar com seguidor é a fonte nova mais barata em 43 dos 48 mercados. O pano de fundo é a fila das turbinas. Conforme o TechCrunch, citado pelo site Mezha, quem monta os maiores data centers tem comprado as turbinas disponíveis. As turbinas a gás de ciclo aberto levam de dois a quatro anos para chegar. A fila das de ciclo combinado vai até o início dos anos 2030. Quanto custa a bateria hoje O custo global de referência de um projeto de bateria de quatro horas caiu 27% em 2025, para US$ 78 por MWh, de acordo com o levantamento de fevereiro da BloombergNEF, citado pelo TaiyangNews. A China puxa a média para baixo. O custo de lá é mais de 55% inferior ao do resto da Ásia-Pacífico, que fica em US$ 134 por MWh. Para a América Latina, a Wood Mackenzie projeta queda de 42% no custo das baterias em escala de rede até 2060. O Brasil não aparece, nos textos abertos sobre o relatório, entre os 43 mercados citados. O relatório completo não está público, então a Wood Mackenzie é lida aqui pelos resumos da imprensa especializada. O Brasil: data centers entram na fila da rede O lado brasileiro já tem número. Em 6 de outubro, o primeiro processo competitivo de acesso à transmissão, o PNAST, alocou os 228 MW que sobravam em quatro pontos de conexão de São Paulo. Os três vencedores são data centers: Pahlavan One, Pahlavan Three e Digital DC Brasil, informou o Canal Solar. Sete projetos disputaram, somando 451 MW. Sobraram 223 MW de pedidos sem espaço na rede. Nesta temporada, o ONS cadastrou 367 empreendimentos de geração e consumo, com mais de 20 GW em solicitações. Quem olha o consumo vê o motivo. O Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia 2036, divulgado em 8 de outubro pelo Ministério de Minas e Energia e pela EPE, estima que os data centers saltem de 3 TWh para 30 TWh em 2036, segundo a Agência Eixos. O consumo total do país vai de 702 TWh para 979 TWh no mesmo período. A conta própria: o consumo cresce 277 TWh (979 menos 702) e os data centers respondem por 27 TWh desse aumento (30 menos 3). Dá cerca de 9,7% de toda a expansão vinda de um único setor. E as baterias no Brasil? O mesmo plano estima que o sistema precise de 9,2 GW de armazenamento em dez anos: 7,2 GW em baterias e 2,0 GW em hidrelétricas reversíveis. Os primeiros leilões de baterias estão marcados para dezembro, com início de fornecimento em agosto de 2028. Há um limite de rede. Em coluna no Canal Solar, Roberto Valer lembra que o leilão recebeu 296 GW de baterias cadastradas, mas nem todas cabem. A nota técnica do ONS de 30 de setembro lista 373 barramentos candidatos. Só 315 têm margem de 30 MW, o mínimo para habilitar um projeto. Quem paga pelas baterias? A Aneel abriu consulta pública, aberta até 9 de novembro, sobre como dividir o custo do leilão de baterias. Pela proposta da área técnica, eólicas, solares e nucleares podem responder pela parcela máxima do encargo, enquanto térmicas e hidrelétricas pagariam percentuais menores. A micro e minigeração distribuída fica fora da base inicial, informou a Cenário Energia. A metodologia final só sai depois do leilão. Quanto desse encargo chegaria à conta de luz do consumidor ainda não foi calculado em nenhum documento aberto, e por isso não há número honesto para dar aqui. O que fica para o leitor Três pontos para acompanhar: a consulta da Aneel até 9 de novembro, o leilão de baterias de 2 e 4 de dezembro e a consulta pública do PDE 2036, aberta até 6 de novembro. A comparação mundial entre baterias e turbinas a gás de pico dá o cenário de custo. Quanto ela vale para o Brasil depende do leilão de baterias e do desenho do encargo.

artigo.texto: BYD's Pakistan Plant Takes Shape as Seagull Pre-Orders Open and Exports Do the Heavy Lifting Published on 10/10/2026 at 03:20 | Editorial boerse-global.de BYD has kicked off reservations for the second generation of its best-selling Seagull compact EV, with the revamped model — now badged the Great Seagull — slated to reach Chinese showrooms before the end of the year. The announcement came a day before the stock closed Friday's European session at EUR 8.65, up 4.2%, though a separate trading update put the shares at EUR 8.61 for a 3.8% gain as a broader rally across Chinese electric-vehicle makers provided additional lift. A Bigger, Punchier Seagull Figures from China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology show the new Seagull stretching to 4,205 mm in length with a 2,650 mm wheelbase — 425 mm and 150 mm more than its predecessor, respectively. Power rises sharply as well: a 95 kW unit now drives the rear axle, replacing the outgoing 55 kW motor. FinDreams, BYD's battery subsidiary, supplies lithium iron phosphate packs in 29.99 kWh and 39.23 kWh capacities, and an optional LiDAR roof sensor will be offered. The outgoing generation ranks among the world's best-selling pure EVs, with more than 212,000 units delivered through August. Management has yet to disclose pricing for the new version. Pakistan Becomes Plant Number Six On the production front, BYD Vice President Liu Xueliang confirmed that assembly operations in Pakistan will begin in the second half of 2026. The facility starts at 25,000 vehicles a year, scalable to 50,000, and will create over 1,100 direct jobs — making it the company's sixth manufacturing site outside China. BYD is also in talks with local partner Mega Motor Company about rolling out ultra-fast charging infrastructure built around the next generation of its in-house Blade battery. Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying BYD? Logistics are expanding in tandem. The automaker has ordered ten more car carriers from China Merchants Industry, each capable of holding 9,200 standard passenger vehicles, bringing its owned fleet to 18 ships by 2029. September Sales and the Export Engine Group-wide, BYD moved 463,561 new-energy vehicles in September, up nearly 17% year on year. The nine-month picture is less flattering: global volumes slipped 3.94% to 3,131,576 units as domestic demand stalled. Overseas shipments of passenger cars and pickups hit 179,877 units in September, a jump of 153.9%, according to agency reports cited by Reuters — growth that has helped offset the soft home market. Europe is emerging as a proving ground. In the UK, BYD logged 20,140 registrations for September, an 80% surge year on year and a 5.76% market share that made it the month's second-strongest brand. Valuation, Analyst Views and the US Question BYD's market capitalization currently stands at roughly EUR 75.72 billion. SDIC Securities International reiterated its buy rating with a target of HKD 103.6, pointing to solid growth prospects. UOB Kay Hian trimmed its sales estimates for Chinese automakers across 2026 to 2028 following the weak first nine months, but kept BYD as a top pick and projected a recovery in 2027. The stock remains down about 19% since the start of the year — a decline of roughly 20% on one reading — leaving investors to weigh whether the recent momentum marks a genuine turning point or just a bounce in a still-difficult market. Geopolitics looms as the biggest obstacle. Executive Vice President Stella Li said yesterday that tensions between major economies represent the foremost hurdle to global expansion, and as a direct consequence the company is holding back from selling passenger cars in the United States for now. Li also ruled out partnerships with other Chinese firms, effectively shutting the world's second-largest auto market out of BYD's revenue base for the foreseeable future. Paris as the Next Test Attention now turns to the Paris Motor Show, running from October 12 to 18, where BYD will unveil a new model at a press conference on the opening day. How the company positions that product offensive for European buyers in the crucial final quarter — and whether export momentum can keep compensating for weakness at home — will shape the next leg of the story. artigo.texto: CATL's capital play is eerily similar to that of NVIDIA. Earning 240 million yuan per day, CATL still believes its battery business is not large enough. After investing 5 billion yuan in June this year to become the second-largest external investor of Deepseek, CATL was recently revealed to have once again led a new round of financing of nearly 100 billion yuan for DeepSeek. This is just the tip of the iceberg of CATL's cross-sector investments. Since 2026, CATL has poured in more than 100 billion yuan, covering AI large models, data centers, HVDC power supply and energy storage systems, and even extended its reach to nuclear fusion. Zeng Yuqun, founder of CATL, once stated his ambition bluntly: to build the "four pillars and eight beams" of the new energy era, and the battery is only one of the pillars; some capabilities cannot be cultivated internally quickly, so the gaps will be filled through mergers and acquisitions. This makes the "Ning King" increasingly similar to NVIDIA in the new energy era. In the AI industry, NVIDIA takes GPUs as the fulcrum, on the one hand investing in model, cloud computing and application companies to expand computing demand and technical cooperation; on the other hand, it closely binds key customers and embeds its computing platform into the entire AI industrial chain. CATL is also taking batteries as the fulcrum, extending its capabilities to computing power, electricity and energy infrastructure through investment and mergers and acquisitions. Transforming from a power battery supplier to the underlying platform of the new energy industry may be a historic opportunity for CATL. Striving for upstream and downstream layout There is a famous scene in the history of China's new energy vehicles: Zeng Qinghong, then chairman of GAC Group, publicly complained that "all car companies are working for CATL". Wu Kai, chief scientist of CATL, immediately complained in response that the company was only "struggling on the edge of profit", pointing the finger at the skyrocketing prices of upstream battery raw materials. Neither car companies nor battery manufacturers were willing to take the blame, and the problem finally fell on a piece of "stone". Key raw materials such as lithium carbonate are important variables affecting the cost of power batteries. However, the mining industry is a typical strong cyclical industry, with prices fluctuating sharply along with the supply and demand cycle. Back in 2022, lithium prices soared all the way, pushing the profit contradictions of the entire industrial chain to the forefront. Perhaps having suffered enough from the pain of "no mines in hand", CATL has accelerated its expansion to the upstream. Through self-construction, equity participation, joint ventures and acquisitions, it has invested in lithium mica projects in Yichun, Jiangxi, spodumene projects in Sichuan, copper and cobalt mines in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, nickel mines in Indonesia and lithium mine projects in Africa, trying to grasp the resources that affect battery costs in its own hands as much as possible. After 2023, as lithium prices went down, CATL's mining investment also shrank to some extent. In April this year, the company announced its plan to establish Times Resource Group with a registered capital of 30 billion yuan to integrate its mining assets under its banner. On the other hand, by taking shares in Jiangxi Shenghua, a subsidiary of lithium iron phosphate supplier Fulin Jinggong, Hunan Yuneng, a phosphate cathode material supplier, and investing in Xinmai Semiconductor, a power management chip supplier, CATL is also strengthening its ties with the supply chain. In the upstream, CATL and NVIDIA do not use the same set of strategies — in the face of manufacturing oligarchs such as TSMC and SK Hynix, NVIDIA mostly uses orders, advance payments and joint development to lock in production capacity; while CATL, facing the more scattered mining and material links with greater cyclical fluctuations, relies more on equity plus long-term agreements. However, when optical communication becomes the new bottleneck of AI clusters, NVIDIA has also begun to invest in Coherent and Lumentum. This means that although their "toolkits" may not be the same, the two chain leaders are highly consistent at their core: The real hegemony of the industrial chain is not only to master the links that others cannot bypass, but also to ensure that you do not have to rely on others that you cannot bypass. If investing in the upstream is to solve the problem of neck sticking and ensure that batteries can be manufactured stably, then making moves in the downstream is to solve the market demand. Power battery is a capital-intensive and not fully standardized business. From production line construction, equipment procurement to commissioning and ramp-up, huge amounts of funds need to be invested in advance; different car models have different requirements for cell specifications, battery pack structure, fast charging and thermal management. If a production line is misaligned, the cost will be huge. To this end, CATL has successively invested in car companies such as AVATR, BAIC New Energy, Zeekr, IM Motors, Neta and Chery. In 2021, it directly contributed 770 million yuan to become the second largest shareholder of AVATR; in addition to equity investment, it also established joint venture battery companies with SAIC, GAC, Geely, Changan, Dongfeng (note: later withdrew) and other car companies, and explored the "factory in factory" cooperation model with Seres. These capital relationships allow CATL to enter the vehicle R&D, procurement and production systems earlier, increase the probability of its batteries being selected, and also raise the cost for car companies to replace suppliers.
