artigo.texto: Sistema ocupa uma área vedada de 2.642 metros quadrados O projeto prevê a instalação do sistema numa área vedada de 2.642 metros quadrados, inserida numa parcela com cerca de 9.279 metros quadrados. Estão previstos 12 contentores de baterias, com capacidade de 5 MWh cada, num total de 60 MWh, e quatro contentores equipados com transformadores e inversores bidirecionais, bem como dois postos de seccionamento. A infraestrutura destina-se ao armazenamento de energia elétrica, permitindo a sua posterior disponibilização à rede. A área impermeabilizada prevista é de cerca de 268 metros quadrados, correspondendo a aproximadamente 10% da área vedada do sistema. Pareceres favoráveis com condições associadas ao projeto A proposta dos serviços municipais é favorável à viabilidade da localização, na sequência dos pareceres e consultas realizados durante a análise do processo. A Comissão de Coordenação e Desenvolvimento Regional do Centro emitiu decisão global favorável, após consulta à Agência Portuguesa do Ambiente e à Autoridade Nacional da Aviação Civil. O Departamento de Ambiente e Sustentabilidade do Município não identificou constrangimentos ambientais à pretensão, tendo definido um conjunto de condições a observar caso o projeto avance para a fase de execução. Entre estas encontra-se a constituição de uma faixa de gestão de combustível com largura não inferior a 100 metros em torno da instalação. A Águas de Coimbra considerou igualmente adequada a solução prevista para a drenagem das águas pluviais, condicionada ao cumprimento das medidas constantes do respetivo parecer. A União das Freguesias de Assafarge e Antanhol não apresentou pronúncia dentro do prazo definido, tendo a ausência de resposta sido considerada favorável nos termos da consulta realizada. A viabilidade da localização fica ainda sujeita ao cumprimento dos requisitos constantes dos pareceres emitidos e dos limiares legalmente aplicáveis ao projeto. A eventual sujeição a Avaliação de Impacte Ambiental (AIA) ou a análise caso a caso será apreciada posteriormente pelas entidades competentes. O limite da parcela coincide parcialmente, em 3,60%, com a área do Plano de Pormenor do iParque – Parque Tecnológico de Coimbra, ficando salvaguardado que essa área não poderá ser ocupada ou utilizada pelo projeto.

artigo.texto: Developer Returns With A Second Proposal For A Zoning Overlay To Facilitate Apartments In Proximity To Pearl River Transit Station The developer of Jefferson Arms, a proposed 88-unit residential project in Pearl River’s CO (Commercial) zone, returned to the Orangetown Town Board last week asking the town board to advance a proposal that would create a Development Enhancement (DE) Overlay Zone in Pearl River’s downtown. The DE Overlay would allow rental apartments on parcels of land of at least one acre in size and within 1,000 feet of the Pearl River commuter train station. The developer first appeared in May, with a proposal that would allow a 4-story building with 109 apartment units and 132 parking spaces at 10 Jefferson Avenue. In a new iteration, the developer scaled back its project to 88 units (65 units per acre) in a three-story building with below ground parking. Jefferson Arms would have 12 studios, 63 1-bedroom units, 12 2-bedroom units, and one three-bedroom unit for a superintendent. The overlay would apply only to CO (Commercial/Office) zoned land, but would not change the zoning. It would act as an overlay to the existing zoning. Any development would still be subject to review by Orangetown’s land use boards. A proposal to create a zoning overlay in proximity to the Metro North/New Jersey Transit line on Main Street would permit the redevelopment of fallow commercial property in Pearl River. While there are only a few CO parcels large enough (over one acre) to avail itself of the development overlay, the developer’s representative told the board that smaller parcels in the CO zone could be assembled to reach the one-acre threshold. In a presentation to the Town Board last week, the developer, Jefferson Arms LLC, touted the benefits in creating housing opportunities for young professionals, commuters, downsizing seniors, and local workforce residents. Benefits also included additional foot traffic for downtown businesses, as well as enhancing the appearance of the area which is dotted with fallow and underutilized commercial lots. Also discussed was the increase in the taxes the CO lots would pay after conversion to residential use. The owner of the site pays about $69,000 annually in taxes. During the presentation, the owner’s representative alluded to tax revenues from the site many times larger than what is currently levied. The board responded that the 1,000 foot proximity did not make sense, as it could effectively divide individual parcels. A suggestion was made to define the boundaries by streets, not distance from the train station. Changes to the zoning code and the creation of overlays are discretionary with the town board. It has no obligation to act on an application. The Board did not make any decision on the overlay, but referred it to the Town Planner, the Town Planning Board, and the County Planning Department for recommendations and input. BESS Developer Seeks Hardship Exemption From Orangetown Moratorium On Data Centers And Battery Energy Storage Systems A developer of a Batter Energy Storage System (BESS) appeared before the Orangetown Town Board asking for a hardship exemption from the Town’s six-month moratorium on data centers and battery energy storage systems. A BESS is an engineered installation of rechargeable batteries tied to a utility substation that stores electrical energy and releases it on demand. Batteries are charged in the evening when power demand is low and released during the day or when power demand peaks. The Town of Orangetown passed a six-month town-wide moratorium on new data centers and battery energy storage systems in August. The moratorium allowed for discretionary hardship exemptions. The Orangetown Battery Project, hosted behind a warehouse at 524 Route 303 in Orangeburg, would install about fifteen 30-foot containers of rechargeable batteries adjacent to the railroad tracks in Orangetown’s LO district. The applicant negotiated a contract with the owner of the property in May 2025 and was approved for interconnection with Orange & Rockland in December. It has met with the Orangetown Planning Board several times prior to the imposition of the moratorium. The project does not require any variances, waivers, or zone changes. The batteries would connect to the O&R substation on Mountainview Road. According to NYSERDA, energy storage strengthens and modernizes the electric grid by making it more flexible, efficient, and resilient—benefiting communities, businesses, and households across New York. Battery storage systems pose a unique fire risk, and advances in containment and suppression help local governments manage the risk. The applicant advised the town board that it intended to create a “host community agreement” that would require the operator to finance any equipment the local fire district needed to address a potential fire risk. The town board was inclined to grant the waiver, but a representative of AKRF, a planning firm retained by the town to evaluate the application sought additional information from the developer. The developer agreed to provide the information and the matter was rolled forward to the next town board meeting on October 20th. There was no public comment either in favor or opposed to the application. artigo.texto: Transnordestina, data centers e atração de novas empresas são prioridades do novo mandato, diz Elmano Em entrevista exclusiva ao O POVO e à rádio O POVO CBN nesta sexta-feira, 9 de outubro, o gestor citou ainda o fortalecimento do agronegócio e o polo automotivo como motores do desenvolvimento do Estado 14:11 | Out. 09, 2026 Transnordestina, data centers e atração de novas empresas serão as prioridades econômicas do novo mandato do governador reeleito do Ceará, Elmano de Freitas (PT), que inicia em 2027. Siga o canal de Economia no WhatsApp para ficar bem informado A informação foi dada em entrevista ao O POVO e à rádio O POVO CBN nesta sexta-feira, 9 de outubro. Sobre a Transnordestina, Elmano citou que a infraestrutura permitirá atrair investimentos para todo o Ceará, com foco principal no Interior. Nesse contexto, destacou que a ferrovia ajudará a transformar a região do Cariri, que engloba 29 municípios do Estado, em um grande polo logístico. Segundo ele, um dos desafios da gestão, no entanto, será descentralizar o desenvolvimento para as demais cidades da região. Elmano afirmou que pretende construir em Missão Velha (município distante 452,89 km de Fortaleza), na Região Metropolitana do Cariri, um porto seco para que o escoamento da produção possa ser realizado no local. Veja dicas rápidas sobre Educação Financeira no Dei Valor “É um desafio nosso porque temos Juazeiro, Crato e Barbalha crescendo. Precisamos pensar em outras cidades do Cariri para crescer de maneira aproximada, com Missão Velha, Campos Sales e outros municípios da microrregião do Cariri também se desenvolvendo”, comentou. O governador também anunciou a meta de integrar a Transnordestina à Ferrovia Norte-Sul, após a finalização das obras. A medida, para ele, permitirá ao Estado acessar a produção de grãos do Centro-Oeste do Brasil, já que a Norte-Sul interliga o Maranhão a São Paulo, passando por Tocantins, Goiás e Minas Gerais. “Nossa prioridade agora é vincularmos a Transnordestina à Ferrovia Norte-Sul, porque nós estaríamos trazendo para o Ceará toda a produção de grãos vindo lá do Centro-Oeste”, destacou. Acompanhe mais notícias de Economia no Linkedin do O POVO O gestor acrescentou que o agronegócio do País será impactado, pois os produtos passarão a contar com quatro portos para exportação: Itaqui (MA), Pecém (CE), Suape (PE) e Santos (SP), este último já integrado à malha ferroviária. O agronegócio também foi citado como prioridade. De acordo com Elmano, a gestão nos próximos quatro anos terá foco no fortalecimento do setor e na melhoria da qualidade de vida do trabalhador do campo. Data centers e a formação de mão de obra Outro ponto destacado foi o avanço tecnológico promovido pelos investimentos na construção de data centers no Estado. Segundo o governador, esses aportes favorecem o ambiente de negócios e a geração de empregos qualificados. Confira os assuntos econômicos no Ceará, no Brasil e no Mundo “Os data centers nos permitem vislumbrar uma ambiência para o desenvolvimento de empresas e a prestação de serviços nas áreas de tecnologia e segurança cibernética, além da formação de mão de obra para esse setor, garantindo empregos e salários melhores”, afirmou. Ceará como um polo automotivo de carro elétrico nacional e internacional No setor industrial, Elmano ressaltou que o Estado, a partir da Planta Automotiva do Ceará (Pace), localizada em Horizonte (a 42 km de Fortaleza), vem se consolidando como polo nacional e internacional de veículos elétricos. Ele revelou que há negociações em curso para a instalação de uma nova empresa no local, com anúncio previsto ainda para este ano. Detalhes sobre a companhia não foram divulgados devido a cláusulas de confidencialidade. Captação de empresas e investimento privado O governador relembrou as tratativas para atrair a produção de bobinas laminadas, classificada por ele como uma “indústria de base essencial para impulsionar outros setores produtivos”. “Queremos que o investimento possa iniciar o mais rápido possível”, pontuou. O planejamento estadual prevê ainda um impulso nos setores de mineração e gás natural, respaldado por convênios com a Universidade Federal do Ceará (UFC) para estudos de viabilidade e confirmação de jazidas minerais. Elmano reforçou, por fim, a necessidade de ampliar os investimentos privados no Estado por meio de maior sinergia de planejamento entre o setor público e a iniciativa privada.

artigo.texto: Researchers develop hybrid materials for more efficient thermal energy storage 'Salogels' combine salt hydrates and polymer structures to store heat reliably, with potential uses in energy-efficient buildings, batteries, smart windows and electronics. Heating and cooling buildings accounts for a large portion of global energy use. Researchers from Texas A&M University are developing a new class of hybrid materials that could help store thermal energy more efficiently for use in buildings and other technologies. The materials, which the research team from the Department of Materials Science and Engineering call salogels, combine inorganic salt hydrates with polymer structures. Salt hydrates can store substantial amounts of thermal energy, absorbing heat during the day and releasing it later as temperatures fall. They are also highly resistant to burning. The main problem is that, on their own, they can leak and break down with repeated use. Introducing a polymer network or structure into them can resolve many of these concerns without sacrificing storage capacity. “Salogels represent a shift from simply storing heat to engineering multifunctional materials that combine thermal energy storage and conversion,” said Dr. Kartik Kumar Rajagopalan, a research scientist in Texas A&M’s Soft Matter Facility (SoMF). “By understanding how polymers interact with salt hydrates at the molecular level, we can begin to design materials with properties tailored for real-world energy applications.” Rajagopalan led the research under the direction of Dr. Svetlana A. Sukhishvili, professor and director of the SoMF. The work was featured on the cover of ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces. Dr. Peiran Wei, SoMF facility manager and senior research scientist, is credited with designing the cover art — the gummy bear-shaped salogel — for the publication’s June 10 issue. The work builds on several years of research by Sukhishvili’s group examining interactions between polymers and salt hydrates. One major finding was that the polymer network changed how the salt hydrates crystallize and helped prevent supercooling. The findings could inform a future machine learning tool used to design new materials with tailored properties. Beyond building uses, the team is exploring applications in batteries and temperature-control electronics, smart windows, anti-icing coatings, supercapacitors and energy conversion systems. Funding came from the National Science Foundation’s Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future program. Rajagopalan said the group’s next steps include improving the mechanical strength of salogels, reducing supercooling further, testing with 3D printing for processing and applying the material to electrochemical energy conversion. More information: Hybrid Polymer–Inorganic Salt Hydrate Materials: Applications for Heat Storage and Beyond DOI: 10.1021/acsami.6c07502 Journal: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces

artigo.texto: Silicon has long been regarded as the most promising successor to graphite in the anodes of lithium-ion batteries, offering a theoretical lithium storage capacity roughly ten times that of the carbon material that has dominated commercial cells for decades. Yet silicon’s Achilles heel has proved stubbornly difficult to overcome: as lithium ions flood into the material during charging, it swells by up to several hundred percent, cracking particles, fracturing electrodes, and consuming electrolyte until the battery fades away after relatively few cycles. A research team at Dalian University of Technology in China now reports a composite anode design that confronts this problem on multiple fronts at once, combining a yolk-double-shell architecture with a porous carbon scaffold derived from bimetallic metal-organic frameworks and doped with nickel-cobalt alloy nanoparticles. The study, published in the journal Ionics by Tuo Zhang, Wei Xiao Dong, Ying Yang, Rui Yi Chen, and Ping Chen of the State Key Laboratory of Fine Chemicals, describes a material synthesized through a sol-gel process paired with a MOF self-templating strategy. The resulting composite places silicon at the core of a nested structure in which internal voids and dual carbon shells give the expanding particle room to breathe. After calcination, the bimetallic nickel-cobalt framework transforms into what the authors describe as a concrete-like porous carbon structure embedded with NiCo alloy, a rigid yet permeable matrix that both cushions mechanical stress and conducts electricity. The electrochemical results reported for the composite are striking. The material retained a specific capacity of 786.1 milliampere-hours per gram after 500 cycles at a current density of 1 ampere per gram, a level of endurance that represents meaningful progress for silicon-based anodes, which frequently lose most of their capacity within far fewer cycles. Equally important for fast-charging applications, the anode delivered an average specific capacity of 335.1 milliampere-hours per gram even at a punishing current density of 5 amperes per gram, indicating that lithium ions and electrons can move through the electrode quickly enough to sustain high-rate operation. To understand why the design works, it helps to consider the mechanics of silicon lithiation. When silicon absorbs lithium, its crystal lattice distorts dramatically, and the resulting expansion generates stresses that pulverize bare silicon particles and detach them from the conductive network. Conventional approaches have wrapped silicon in carbon shells, but a rigid shell that is too thin ruptures, while one that is too thick adds dead weight and impedes lithium transport. The yolk-shell concept takes a different route: by deliberately leaving void space between the silicon core and its surrounding shells, the structure accommodates expansion internally, allowing the outer architecture to remain intact and electrically connected cycle after cycle. The bimetallic MOF component adds a second layer of engineering sophistication. Metal-organic frameworks are crystalline lattices of metal nodes linked by organic struts, prized for their enormous internal surface areas and tunable chemistry. When a nickel-cobalt MOF is heated under the conditions used in this synthesis, the organic linkers carbonize while the metal nodes aggregate into alloy nanoparticles dispersed throughout the resulting porous carbon. In the composite anode, this transformation yields a carbon scaffold reinforced with conductive NiCo alloy, which the researchers compare to concrete for its combination of structural robustness and porosity. The alloy phases raise the electrical conductivity of the carbon matrix, shortening the pathways that electrons and lithium ions must travel, while the open pore network facilitates electrolyte diffusion deep into the electrode. The choice of two metals rather than one is also deliberate. Nickel and cobalt alloys have established track records in electrochemical applications, and bimetallic frameworks allow researchers to tune properties such as catalytic activity, conductivity, and structural stability in ways that single-metal systems cannot easily match. In the context of a silicon anode, the alloy-doped carbon serves as more than passive reinforcement; it helps maintain an unbroken electronic network around particles that are constantly swelling and contracting, a dynamic environment that would quickly isolate more brittle conductive phases. The synthesis route itself may prove as consequential as the performance numbers. By using the MOF as a self-template, the team avoids elaborate multi-step nanofabrication, letting the framework’s inherent geometry dictate the final architecture as it converts to porous carbon during calcination. Combined with the sol-gel preparation of the silicon-carbon precursor, the process offers a scalable path toward composite anodes whose internal structure is engineered at the nanometer scale without requiring exotic equipment. The authors suggest that this design philosophy provides new ideas for the development of anode materials for lithium-ion batteries, a field where manufacturing practicality often determines whether laboratory breakthroughs reach production lines. The broader context underscores the stakes. Silicon anodes are already beginning to appear in commercial lithium-ion cells, typically blended with graphite at low percentages to extend driving range in electric vehicles without sacrificing cycle life. Every improvement in silicon’s stability translates directly into batteries that hold more energy per kilogram and charge faster, qualities that automakers and consumer electronics manufacturers are racing to exploit. artigo.texto: Yandex Go taxi and delivery services in Kazakhstan have been disrupted for 36 hours following a drone attack on Russian technology giant Yandex’s data center in Vladimir, leaving users, drivers and couriers unable to access the app. "Yandex Go services are currently operating with errors or may be temporarily unavailable," the company’s Kazakhstan press service said. "We cannot yet name exact timelines, but we are doing everything possible to bring them back as soon as possible." The outage shows how Ukraine’s apparent campaign against Yandex data centers in Russia is spilling into neighboring countries that rely on the company’s services, including Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Belarus and Armenia. Yandex Go Kazakhstan said personal data of Kazakh users is stored on servers in Kazakhstan, but that its services rely on distributed infrastructure. "Individual technological components may be located on servers in different countries. Therefore, technical problems in one component can affect service availability in several countries," it said. The company did not directly confirm that the outage was caused by the attack in Russia. Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development announced Sunday that the servers holding users' personal data were in the country and working normally, but some key components for taxi and delivery services are abroad. It said it was working with Yandex and local providers to restore services. In Uzbekistan, Yandex said some Yandex Go services were unavailable or working intermittently, without saying whether the problem was linked to the attack. Services in Kyrgyzstan were working normally, Russian media outlet TASS reported. Yandex said search, its Alisa voice assistant, maps, mail and taxi services were gradually being restored in Russia, though some functions remain unavailable. The company limited some features of its Disk cloud storage. "We deliberately limited some functions of Yandex 360, including Disk, to preserve the main thing, the operability of services," Yandex told RBC. Yandex said it agreed with cloud providers VK Cloud, Selectel and K2Cloud to quickly host clients’ data and services. Its shares fell more than 5% in early trading on the Moscow Exchange on Monday, TASS reported. Replacing damaged equipment could take about six months, market sources told Kommersant. "These were very large data centers, and since their construction, a global shortage and rising prices for computing capacity began, especially for AI accelerators. Equipping them promises to be expensive and long," said Sergey Kudryashov of Strategy Partners. Russia’s Digital Development Minister Maksut Shadaev said his ministry and the Defense Ministry are working on protecting data centers, TASS reported. Drones struck Yandex data centers in Sasovo in the Ryazan region on Oct. 8, Kaluga on Oct. 9 and Vladimir on Oct. 11, shutting the Vladimir facility completely. Yandex has five data centers, four in Russia and one in Finland that was disconnected because of sanctions. "Two can play at this game," Andriy Kovalenko, former head of Ukraine’s Center for Countering Disinformation, wrote after the first strike, as the Yandex outage spreads beyond Russia.

The global Energy Storage Chemicals Market is entering a phase of industrial scaling and optimization, driven by the twin engines of electric vehicle (EV) adoption and stationary grid storage deployment. This market encompasses the core chemical components and materials used in electrochemical energy storage systems, including cathode active materials, anode materials, electrolytes, and separators. As the world transitions toward cleaner energy and transportation, demand for these performance-critical chemicals is set to accelerate through 2035. The market is not a commodity chemical play but an application-specific materials ecosystem where formulation and purity directly dictate system-level energy density, cycle life, safety, and project bankability. Demand is bifurcating between high-volume, cost-optimized chemistries for mass-market EVs and grid storage, and specialized, higher-margin formulations for extreme environments and long-duration applications. Supply security has emerged as a paramount concern, driving vertical integration, long-term offtake agreements, and geopolitical re-shoring of precursor and active material production. The qualification cycle for new chemical formulations remains a critical bottleneck, extending 18-36 months, which protects incumbents with proven supply histories. Regulatory landscapes are evolving from passive safety standards to active performance mandates and sustainability criteria, adding compliance costs and differentiation opportunities. This report provides a structured, commercially grounded analysis of the market, covering historical data from 2012 to 2025 and forward-looking scenarios through 2035. The baseline scenario for the Energy Storage Chemicals Market forecasts robust growth from 2026 to 2035, with a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.5%, reaching a market index of 325 (2025=100) by 2035. This outlook is underpinned by sustained demand from the automotive and e-mobility sector, which accounts for the largest share of consumption, as well as rapid expansion in grid-scale and renewable integration storage projects. The market is expected to benefit from declining battery costs, supportive government policies, and corporate sustainability commitments. However, growth will be tempered by supply chain bottlenecks, particularly in lithium and nickel refining, and by the lengthy qualification cycles for new chemistries. Regionally, Asia-Pacific will maintain its dominance in both production and consumption, driven by China's massive battery manufacturing base. North America and Europe are expected to gain share as localization efforts and regulatory mandates accelerate. The market will see a shift toward higher-nickel cathodes for EVs and lithium iron phosphate (LFP) for stationary storage, with sodium-ion and solid-state technologies emerging as niche alternatives by 2035. Pricing will remain volatile due to raw material supply-demand imbalances, but overall value will migrate toward higher-performance, application-specific formulations. Strategic imperatives include securing raw material supply, investing in recycling and circular economy, and developing chemistries that enhance safety and cycle life. The automotive and e-mobility sector is the largest consumer of energy storage chemicals, primarily for lithium-ion battery manufacturing. As EV production targets escalate globally, demand for cathode active materials, anode materials, electrolytes, and separators will surge. The shift toward higher-nickel chemistries for longer range and faster charging will increase the need for high-purity nickel and cobalt compounds. Simultaneously, the adoption of LFP for entry-level EVs will drive demand for iron phosphate and lithium carbonate. Demand-side indicators include EV sales penetration rates, battery pack sizes, and government mandates phasing out internal combustion engines. artigo.texto: Ricardo – AMBERS is green light for next wave of battery technology in high performance vehicles Advanced modular battery technology (AMBERS) continues to make hybrid powertrain adoption easier and more affordable across high performance applications. Ricardo’s innovative AMBERS programme is supporting this drive. Dr Temoc Rodriguez, Ricardo’s Global Technology Lead for battery development, tells us more. “This move is being driven by multiple factors, including a more conscious approach to the environment, but also the evolution of electrification and hybrid technologies to improve performance levels over traditional propulsion systems. “Innovation has always been at the forefront of motorsport and high performance vehicles, with many of these technologies filtering down into mainstream applications. However, the switch to electrified propulsion systems has been slower to catch on. “Nonetheless, things are changing, in part due to more advanced battery technology and electric drives, leading hybrid vehicles to deliver instant torque, high energy efficiency and advanced energy management. “Although, we’re still a long way from parity across motorsport classes.” Q: What are the main challenges to wider adoption in motorsport applications? “Cost is one of the biggest factors shaping decisions in motorsport, and has been a barrier influencing the wider adoption of battery technology in the industry. “If you take the pinnacle of the motorsport industry, Formula 1®, the teams are investing huge sums of money in technologies to remain competitive and meet aggressive vehicle targets. “This compares to the other race classes, who have significantly less money to invest. It doesn’t mean that they are less inventive or innovative, but the reality is that they have to manage their budgets in a way that prioritising more off-the-shelf components as opposed to bespoke, or even clean sheet designs. “This is one of the main reasons why different classes of motorsport haven’t witnessed more rapid hybridisation.” Q: How does AMBERS offer a solution? “AMBERS (Advanced modular battery technology) is a platform that has been developed and designed to provide high performance power for hybrid powertrains across all race classes, where something off-the-shelf is needed, without compromising performance. “Ricardo has developed AMBERS as part of a consortium, alongside battery assembler Hyperbat and cell supplier Volklec. The design is Ricardo IP, we own the architecture and can modify it based on individual customer requirements if required. However, it’s been developed as a modular platform, with the intention to make it off-the-shelf and available by the end of 2028. “The modular design lends itself to modifications, including the number of modules in the pack, to fit customer requirements more closely, based around voltage, power and energy, so it’s fully scalable. “It provides a solution, without the need for teams to pay the design, development and test related costs of something bespoke.” “AMBERS is designed to operate across high performance platforms. The pack itself will give users very high current discharge, which supports rapid acceleration and regenerative braking. It’s enabled with a clever integrated thermal management system and it’s also modular, making it fully scalable, based on customer requirements. “Very few off-the-shelf comparisons can be made, based on design, integration and performance capabilities. “In terms of baseline design, performance levels will be dependent on the battery cell that is installed, which will enable performance at a reasonable price. The more powerful the cell, the more expensive the unit becomes. That’s the customisable aspect of AMBERS; cells can be chosen based on the power and cost requirements of the customer – yet the architecture remains the same. Companies can buy AMBERS as an off-the-shelf kit and integrate it into their racing vehicles. “There’s also an opportunity for parallel applications, including in niche and boutique vehicles, both hybrid and fully electric.” Q: What are the next steps for AMBERS? “We’ll have the first prototypes available in 2027, then production is planned to start by the end of 2028, which fits with planned design and development cycles associated with these markets. “Beside the advanced thermal management system, one of our key differentiators will be in our management of the wireless communications in the unit, allowing the sensing electronics to talk to the control module more easily. This eliminates the need for low voltage harnessing. We’ve also looked at how we can improve the BMS system, using artificial intelligence estimation algorithms.” Temoc will be presenting on the AMBERS programme at the upcoming PMW Expo on 11th November 2026 in Cologne, Germany. To learn more you can also visit the Ricardo stand 3072, and talk to the team directly. artigo.texto: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners committed more than €270 million to Kilmarnock South, a 350 MW / 1,400 MWh battery energy storage project in southern Scotland. The investment is being made through Copenhagen Infrastructure IV, the firm’s fourth flagship fund. CIP has taken a final investment decision on the project, and construction is underway. Commercial operations are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2028. Kilmarnock South is designed as a four-hour-duration lithium-ion battery energy storage system. Once operational, it is expected to become the longest-duration battery storage asset in CIP’s U.K. portfolio. The project will store excess Scottish wind power that might otherwise be curtailed and return that electricity to the grid when network capacity is available. Kilmarnock South represents CIP’s fourth investment in transmission-connected battery energy storage in Scotland. The project joins Coalburn 1, Coalburn 2, and Devilla. Coalburn 1 reached commercial operations in August 2026. When all four projects are fully commissioned, CIP’s Scottish battery storage portfolio is expected to provide 1.85 GW of power capacity and 4.4 GWh of energy storage. CIP said that level of storage represents nearly one-third of Great Britain’s current operational battery energy storage capacity. The portfolio would have enough energy storage capacity to meet the electricity demand of more than 5.5 million households for two hours. Kilmarnock South was developed by Noriker Power, which will continue managing the project’s construction phase. The project also has an optimization agreement with Shell Energy Europe designed to provide long-term contracted revenue. KEY QUOTES: “CIP is pleased to add Kilmarnock South to our growing portfolio of UK battery projects, which, once commissioned, will be the longest-duration BESS asset in our UK fleet. Well-sited battery energy storage projects provide valuable power system flexibility which enables the full benefits of low-cost renewables to be captured, strengthening security of supply and helping to both cut and stabilise energy bills for consumers.” Nischal Agarwal, Partner at Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners “A former coal mine at Coalburn is now home to one of Europe’s largest batteries storing clean power, while at Kilmarnock South, a new GBP 232 million battery will store even more Scottish wind power for when it’s needed most. Together, these projects mean less homegrown power going to waste, greater energy security, and lower bills over the long term.” Michael Shanks, U.K. Energy Minister

JEDDAH: Saudi Arabia can supply electricity to AI data centers faster than the US, giving it an edge in attracting computing investments through its advanced power infrastructure and clear plans to expand generation capacity, Siemens Energy CEO Christian Bruch has said. Speaking to Mohammed Fathi of Asharq Bloomberg at the company’s Dammam facility, Bruch said the speed of power delivery has become a key factor in competing for AI projects. He added that advancing or delaying a data center’s launch by six months can make a significant difference as artificial intelligence and superintelligence technologies develop rapidly. Asked whether the Kingdom could supply electricity to data centers faster than the US, Bruch said: “Yes, I think so.” He noted that Saudi Arabia had made significant progress in developing its power infrastructure in recent years and had a clear, coordinated plan for adding new generation capacity. This comes as the company invests around $150 million to expand its Dammam facility, adding 60,000 sq. meters and establishing a factory for large power transformers. The expansion is also expected to create around 130 to 150 additional jobs, as the company seeks to strengthen local manufacturing, serve Saudi demand and export to international markets. Saudi Arabia’s planning and execution advantage Bruch described Saudi Arabia as “a model for strategic infrastructure planning,” saying its clear targets through 2030 and defined electricity generation requirements help suppliers plan and deliver projects in phases, making the process more straightforward than in other countries. He said the Kingdom could also supply electricity to data centers at “highly competitive” costs, enhancing its appeal to companies seeking locations for their investments. Data center operators would find Saudi Arabia a suitable location for their projects, he added, noting that the US “will not always remain the only destination.” Asked about discussions with Humain, Bruch did not disclose any specific agreements but said he expected further announcements on larger-scale, higher-capacity data center computing projects in Saudi Arabia. He added that Siemens Energy’s role is to supply equipment, while other entities would handle operations. Major transformer factory planned for Dammam The Dammam expansion marks another step in Siemens Energy’s industrial development in the Kingdom. The company began with a gas turbine factory, later added compressors for the oil and gas sector, and opened a facility for electrical switchgear used in the power grid last year, according to Bruch. He noted that the new transformer factory would be one of the company’s key manufacturing facilities in this field globally, with production capacity sufficient to serve both the Saudi market and international markets. He added that a further expansion phase could be implemented in the future if business develops in line with the company’s expectations. Bruch did not specify the plant’s annual production capacity but said it would manufacture large power transformers for high-voltage networks, including Saudi Arabia’s main 380-kilovolt transmission grid. He further said: “What we need is clarity on the stability of the environment — in other words, is there sustained demand? Is there a long-term strategy? And that is what I see in Saudi Arabia today.” The investment builds on Siemens Energy’s major contracts in the Kingdom. In June 2024, the company announced a deal worth around $1.5 billion to supply key technologies for the Taiba 2 and Qassim 2 gas-fired power plants, alongside a 25-year maintenance agreement. Each plant is planned to have a capacity of approximately 2,000 megawatts and will use HL-class gas turbines, steam turbines and generators. In March 2025, Siemens Energy announced a further $1.6 billion contract to supply key technologies for the Rumah 2 and Al-Nairyah 2 power plants, with a combined capacity of 3.6 gigawatts. The deal includes 25-year maintenance agreements. At the time, the company said key components for the plants would be manufactured at its Dammam facility. The plants were scheduled to begin connecting to the grid in simple-cycle mode in 2027, before transitioning to full combined-cycle operation the following year, according to the timeline announced at the time. artigo.texto: Mercado global de produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Mercado global de produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia acelera com demanda de veículos elétricos e redes, rumo à expansão até 2035 Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia, o mercado inicia 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia entra em uma fase de escala industrial e otimização, impulsionado pelos dois motores da adoção de veículos elétricos (VEs) e da implantação de armazenamento estacionário em redes elétricas. Esse mercado abrange os principais componentes químicos e materiais usados em sistemas eletroquímicos de armazenamento de energia, incluindo materiais ativos de cátodo, materiais de ânodo, eletrólitos e separadores. À medida que o mundo avança rumo a uma energia e um transporte mais limpos, a demanda por esses produtos químicos críticos para o desempenho deve se acelerar até 2035. Não se trata de um mercado de commodities químicas, mas de um ecossistema de materiais específicos para aplicações, no qual formulação e pureza determinam diretamente a densidade energética em nível de sistema, a vida útil em ciclos, a segurança e a bancabilidade dos projetos. A demanda se divide entre químicas de alto volume e custo otimizado para veículos elétricos de grande consumo e armazenamento em rede, e formulações especializadas de maior margem para ambientes extremos e aplicações de longa duração. A segurança do suprimento tornou-se uma preocupação primordial, impulsionando integração vertical, acordos de compra de longo prazo e relocalização geopolítica da produção de precursores e materiais ativos. O ciclo de qualificação de novas formulações químicas continua sendo um gargalo crítico, estendendo-se por 18 a 36 meses, o que protege os incumbentes com histórico comprovado de fornecimento. Os panoramas regulatórios evoluem de padrões passivos de segurança para mandatos ativos de desempenho e critérios de sustentabilidade, acrescentando custos de conformidade e oportunidades de diferenciação. Este relatório oferece uma análise estruturada e comercialmente fundamentada do mercado, abrangendo dados históricos de 2012 a 2025 e cenários prospectivos até 2035. O cenário-base para o mercado de produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia projeta crescimento robusto de 2026 a 2035, com taxa de crescimento anual composta (CAGR) de 12,5%, alcançando um índice de mercado de 325 (2025=100) até 2035. Essa perspectiva é sustentada pela demanda contínua do setor automotivo e de mobilidade elétrica, que responde pela maior parcela do consumo, bem como pela rápida expansão de projetos de armazenamento em escala de rede e de integração de renováveis. Espera-se que o mercado se beneficie da queda dos custos das baterias, de políticas governamentais de apoio e de compromissos corporativos de sustentabilidade. No entanto, o crescimento será moderado por gargalos na cadeia de suprimentos, especialmente no refino de lítio e níquel, e pelos longos ciclos de qualificação de novas químicas. Regionalmente, a Ásia-Pacífico manterá sua dominância tanto na produção quanto no consumo, impulsionada pela enorme base de fabricação de baterias da China. América do Norte e Europa devem ganhar participação à medida que esforços de localização e mandatos regulatórios se acelerarem. O mercado verá uma mudança em direção a cátodos com maior teor de níquel para veículos elétricos e fosfato de ferro-lítio (LFP) para armazenamento estacionário, com tecnologias de sódio-íon e de estado sólido emergindo como alternativas de nicho até 2035. Os preços permanecerão voláteis devido a desequilíbrios entre oferta e demanda de matérias-primas, mas o valor geral migrará para formulações de maior desempenho e específicas para aplicações. Entre os imperativos estratégicos estão garantir o suprimento de matérias-primas, investir em reciclagem e economia circular e desenvolver químicas que aumentem a segurança e a vida útil em ciclos. Motores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Motores da Demanda - Crescimento acelerado das metas globais de produção e das taxas de adoção de veículos elétricos, impulsionando a demanda por materiais ativos de cátodo e eletrólitos de alto desempenho. - Aumento da implantação de projetos de armazenamento em escala de rede e de integração de renováveis, apoiado por incentivos governamentais e pela queda dos custos das baterias. - Avanços tecnológicos em químicas de baterias, como NMC com alto teor de níquel e sódio-íon, que exigem formulações químicas especializadas. - Iniciativas de localização e relocalização da cadeia de suprimentos na América do Norte e na Europa, ampliando a demanda regional por produtos químicos para armazenamento de energia. - Normas rigorosas de segurança e desempenho, incluindo rastreamento de pegada de carbono e exigências de conteúdo reciclado, impulsionando a demanda por produtos químicos em conformidade. - Expansão da eletrônica de consumo e de aplicações industriais que exigem soluções confiáveis de armazenamento de energia. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Volatilidade dos preços de matérias-primas, especialmente lítio, níquel e cobalto, afetando custos e margens de produção química. - Ciclos longos de qualificação de novas formulações químicas, de 18 a 36 meses, que retardam a entrada no mercado e a adoção de inovações. - Tensões geopolíticas e restrições comerciais que desorganizam as cadeias globais de suprimento e o acesso a mine

artigo.texto: A $750 million investment agreement for industrial development and a potential data center at New River Valley Commerce Park is off, at least for now, after a company did not finalize the contract. The 475-acre site in Pulaski County was scheduled to exchange ownership on Oct. 5, between multi-government representative Virginia’s First Regional Industrial Facility Authority and developer New River Valley LLC, according to the proposed agreement. “Right now as it stands, the contract has expired with the company,” said Michael Solomon, the authority’s executive director. “They had until the 5th to close, and they didn’t.” Solomon said Friday he did not know the reason or reasons for the company’s decision. The initial amount the developer was set to pay was approximately $1.6 million, with $580,000 already in escrow as a deposit. The remaining amount was due at closing, according to Solomon. The authority is likely to get the money that remains in escrow based on the contract, he said. Over 10 years, the developer would have been required to invest at least $750 million in industrial projects such as manufacturing and a data center. No end user for a data center development had been identified, Solomon said. The authority, which owns and manages the commerce park, was created in 1998 through a partnership between 11 member governments — the counties of Bland, Craig, Giles, Montgomery, Pulaski, and Roanoke, the cities of Radford and Roanoke, and the towns of Dublin, Pearisburg and Pulaski. In the efforts to boost economic activity, each member would receive proportional tax revenue from industry development at the site based on the amount of previous investment — host Pulaski County would receive the most. As Cardinal News previously reported, the county was expected to receive $15 million in 2025 from the state’s general funds, appropriated by the General Assembly to go toward utility infrastructure development at the park. That figure was later reduced to $7.5 million, which remains untouched and has carried over into this year’s budget, Solomon said. No new developer has been identified, Solomon said, and the authority continues to assess what other options are available. Cardinal News reached out to New River Valley LLC for comment and did not receive a response last week. The authority will hold a public meeting to discuss data centers in general at the New River Valley Fairgrounds at 5581 Fair Grounds Circle in Dublin from 6 to 8 p.m. Thursday. Christopher Lloyd, senior vice president and director for infrastructure and economic development at McGuireWoods Consulting, is scheduled to speak at the forum. Live questions will not be taken during the meeting and should be presubmitted to executivedirector@nrvcommerpark.org, according to the online event page.

The global Energy Storage High Voltage Connector market is entering a phase of sustained expansion, underpinned by the rapid deployment of grid-scale and large commercial battery energy storage systems (BESS). Supply chain resilience remains a concern due to dependencies on high-conductivity alloys and performance polymers, and long qualification cycles create barriers to entry. artigo.texto: DCF Global: Five Markets Redrawing the AI Infrastructure Map Key Highlights - Spain's Aragón region has attracted more than €60 billion in prospective digital infrastructure investment, but its accelerated permitting model now faces growing scrutiny over water, power, and public participation. - China is rapidly expanding its data center footprint around energy-rich regions such as Inner Mongolia, even as advanced semiconductor availability and computing utilization complicate its AI ambitions. - India has reached approximately 1.75 GW of operational data center capacity, backed by enormous investment commitments, while electricity reliability and infrastructure delivery remain critical concerns. - Latin America's largest data center markets grew 41.3% year over year, led by explosive expansion in Querétaro, Mexico, as Brazil moves to tie investment incentives to sustainability and domestic computing development. - Singapore and Southeast Asia are creating a new regional infrastructure geography, combining selective capacity expansion in Singapore with gigawatt-scale development pipelines in Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. The next phase of the artificial intelligence infrastructure boom is increasingly taking shape far beyond the established data center corridors of Northern Virginia, Dallas, Phoenix, and Silicon Valley. Across Europe, Asia, and Latin America, governments are revising development policies, utilities are confronting enormous new electrical loads, and investors are committing unprecedented amounts of capital to the facilities that will support cloud computing and AI. But the international expansion is not following a single blueprint. In northeastern Spain, regional authorities have turned faster permitting into a competitive advantage, drawing tens of billions of euros in prospective hyperscale investment. Across China's Inner Mongolia region, developers are taking advantage of inexpensive electricity and land to build computing infrastructure at extraordinary scale. In India, a surge of capital commitments is accelerating development while exposing the difficulties of supplying dependable power to a rapidly expanding digital economy. Latin America, meanwhile, is witnessing a major concentration of hyperscale growth around established industrial and connectivity hubs, alongside government efforts to make data center investment serve broader economic objectives. And across Southeast Asia, Singapore's tightly managed infrastructure market is helping shape a wider development ecosystem extending into Malaysia and Indonesia, even as Thailand establishes its own large-scale growth trajectory. These developments share a common underlying tension. To wit: the global appetite for AI computing capacity is apparently growing faster than the infrastructure systems required to support it can consistently be delivered. Of course, a growing pipeline of announced projects does not necessarily translate into operating facilities. Installed electrical capacity does not automatically yield useful AI computing capacity. And government support for data center investment does not eliminate the constraints imposed by power generation, transmission infrastructure, water availability, network connectivity, or public opposition. Those distinctions are becoming increasingly important as developers and investors assess where the next generation of digital infrastructure can actually be built. For the inaugural installment of DCF Global, these five international markets illustrate how the global data center economy is being reorganized around the intersection of capital, energy, geography, and public policy. Spain: The Power of Permitting Meets the Limits of Public Acceptance Spain's Aragón region has emerged as one of Europe's most consequential data center development markets, demonstrating how permitting policy can alter the geography of hyperscale investment. The northeastern region offers available land, substantial renewable energy resources, and access to European telecommunications networks. But its defining competitive advantage may be administrative rather than geographic. An October 6 Reuters investigation detailed how Aragón's streamlined approval processes have helped attract more than €60 billion, approximately $68 billion, in expected data center and digital infrastructure investment over the coming decade. At the center of that strategy is the Project of General Interest of Aragón designation, known as PIGA, which can compress permitting timelines for qualifying developments to less than a year. For hyperscale operators accustomed to lengthy and unpredictable approvals, the potential savings in time and development costs are substantial. Amazon Web Services has outlined approximately €33.7 billion in regional investment plans, while Microsoft has identified potential investments approaching €10 billion. Spanish real estate developer Merlin Properties is also advancing major projects. These figures represent expected or proposed investment, not completed construction or capital already deployed. Nevertheless, their scale illustrates the commercial value of regulatory certainty. But Aragón's success has brought growing scrutiny. Al Jazeera's The Listening Post examines the rapid expansion of data center development in Spain's Aragón region, including the economic opportunities, environmental concerns, and questions of public oversight accompanying billions in hyperscale investment. Environmental groups have challenged whether accelerated reviews adequately account for electricity demand, water consumption, and the consequences of concentrating large industrial loads in local communities. Critics also question whether shortened consultation periods provide meaningful opportunities for public participation. artigo.texto: Mercado global de memória não volátil: Tamanho, Tendências e Previsão até 2035 - Relatório completo em PDF · pacote de dados Excel · documento Word · apresentação executiva - Entrega por e-mail 24/7, inclusive fins de semana e feriados - Copiar e colar habilitado · formato pronto para impressão - Rodadas ilimitadas de esclarecimentos após a entrega Previsão do mercado de memória não volátil até 2035: demanda de data centers e do setor automotivo impulsionará o crescimento Resumo De acordo com o mais recente relatório da IndexBox sobre o mercado global de Memória Não Volátil, o setor entra em 2026 com fundamentos de demanda mais amplos, comportamento de compra mais disciplinado e uma arquitetura de oferta mais diversificada regionalmente. O mercado global de memória não volátil (NVM) é um pilar fundamental da economia digital, pois garante a persistência de dados em dispositivos e infraestruturas. Em 2026, o setor já amadureceu para além da eletrônica de consumo e se tornou indispensável em armazenamento corporativo, infraestrutura de nuvem, sistemas automotivos e IoT industrial. A transição da arquitetura NAND planar para a 3D NAND sustentou a Lei de Moore e viabilizou armazenamento em escala de terabytes, enquanto tecnologias emergentes, como a memória de classe de armazenamento, borram as fronteiras entre memória e armazenamento. Este relatório traz uma análise abrangente do estado atual do mercado e projeta sua trajetória até 2035. O cenário é moldado pela demanda transformadora de setores centrados em dados, pela inovação tecnológica e pela interação entre a dinâmica das cadeias de suprimento e fatores geopolíticos. Entre os principais vetores de demanda estão o crescimento exponencial da criação de dados, a proliferação de cargas de trabalho de IA e aprendizado de máquina, a eletrificação e a automação de veículos e a expansão dos dispositivos de IoT. O mercado, porém, também enfrenta restrições, como a alta intensidade de capital, a ciclicidade e a concentração da cadeia de suprimentos. A análise disseca essas dinâmicas técnicas e comerciais e oferece uma visão clara das forças que moldam produção, demanda, preços e estratégias competitivas. Insights estratégicos são essenciais para fabricantes de memória, OEMs, investidores e formuladores de políticas que atuam nesse mercado intensivo em capital e estrategicamente sensível. O cenário-base para o mercado global de memória não volátil entre 2026 e 2035 prevê crescimento robusto, impulsionado pela demanda estrutural por armazenamento e processamento de dados. A expectativa é de expansão a uma taxa de crescimento anual composta (CAGR) de 7,2%, alcançando um índice de mercado de 200 em 2035 (2025=100). Esse crescimento se apoia no aumento incessante da geração de dados, na migração para computação em nuvem e de borda e na proliferação de aplicações de IA e aprendizado de máquina que exigem memória de alta velocidade e alta capacidade. No segmento de data centers, os SSDs corporativos vêm substituindo os HDDs, impulsionados pela necessidade de acesso mais rápido e menor latência. O setor automotivo desponta como um importante motor de crescimento, com sistemas avançados de assistência ao motorista (ADAS), entretenimento a bordo e direção autônoma exigindo grandes volumes de NVM para armazenamento de código e registro de dados. A eletrônica de consumo, incluindo smartphones e PCs, continua a demandar capacidades de armazenamento maiores, enquanto os dispositivos de IoT se multiplicam e exigem NVM embarcada de baixo consumo. Do lado da oferta, o setor é marcado por alta intensidade de capital e uma base de produção concentrada, sobretudo na Ásia-Pacífico. Avanços tecnológicos, como a transição para 3D NAND com mais camadas e a comercialização de tipos emergentes de NVM, como MRAM e PCM, moldarão o cenário competitivo. O mercado, no entanto, não está livre de desafios. Ciclicidade, tensões geopolíticas e possíveis rupturas na cadeia de suprimentos representam riscos. O cenário-base pressupõe que não haverá grandes recessões globais e que o ritmo de adoção tecnológica será constante. Também considera que as políticas comerciais permanecerão relativamente estáveis, permitindo o fluxo contínuo de componentes e produtos acabados. Nessas condições, o mercado está preparado para expansão sustentada, com o valor migrando para soluções de maior densidade e desempenho. Vetores e Restrições da Demanda Principais Vetores de Demanda - Crescimento exponencial da criação global de dados e necessidade de infraestrutura de armazenamento eficiente. - Proliferação de cargas de trabalho de IA e aprendizado de máquina, que exigem memória de alta largura de banda e baixa latência. - Eletrificação e automação automotiva, com sistemas ADAS e de entretenimento a bordo demandando NVM de grau automotivo. - Expansão de dispositivos de IoT e computação de borda, impulsionando a demanda por NVM embarcada de baixo consumo. - Migração de HDDs para SSDs em data centers e dispositivos de consumo, elevando a demanda por NAND flash. - Implantação do 5G e aumento da capacidade de armazenamento em smartphones, ampliando o conteúdo de NAND e NOR flash por dispositivo. Possíveis Restrições ao Crescimento - Alta intensidade de capital e ciclicidade do mercado de memória semicondutora. - Tensões geopolíticas e restrições comerciais que afetam cadeias de suprimento e acesso à tecnologia. - Concentração da produção em poucas regiões, expondo o mercado a desastres naturais e rupturas logísticas. - Desafios tecnológicos para escalar a 3D NAND além das contagens atuais de camadas e para comercializar tipos emergentes de NVM. - Volatilidade de preços decorrente de desequilíbrios entre oferta e demanda e de ajustes de estoque. artigo.texto: - Category - Defense Tech Three Yandex Data Centers Hit in Four Days—Now All of Its Supercomputers May Be Down A series of Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data centers may have knocked all three of Yandex’s supercomputers offline, potentially taking out half of the six largest supercomputing systems operating in Russia, Russian technology outlet T-Invariant reported on October 11. The first strike came overnight on October 8 against Yandex’s Sasovo data center in Russia’s Ryazan region. The facility, operating since 2014, hosts two of the company’s three supercomputers—Chervonenkis, with a peak performance of 29.42 petaflops, and Lyapunov, rated at 20.03 petaflops. We bring you stories from the ground. Your support keeps our team in the field. Chervonenkis is Yandex’s most powerful machine and had been Russia’s strongest newly built supercomputer of the past 15 years. When it entered service in 2021, it ranked 19th in the global TOP500 list. It has since fallen into the second hundred as sanctions and limited access to advanced hardware made infrastructure upgrades increasingly difficult. A second strike followed on October 9 against Yandex’s data center in Kaluga, located in the Grabtsevo industrial park. Yandex describes the site as its largest data center and one of the biggest such facilities in Russia. Two days later, on October 11, another strike hit the company’s Vladimir data center, home to its third supercomputer, Galushkin, which has a peak performance of 20.64 petaflops. According to T-Invariant, all three Yandex supercomputers are now out of service. Experts interviewed by the outlet said the attacks may have caused enormous damage to Russia’s high-performance computing infrastructure, particularly because the facilities were built long before physical protection against drone strikes became a serious consideration. “Yandex built its centers and supercomputers in peacetime and for peacetime. All development focused on normal human life; nobody imagined drones would hit the roof. Earthquakes and other natural disasters are not expected in the Ryazan and Vladimir regions, so nobody thought about investing in physical protection for the buildings,” one supercomputing expert told the outlet. Yandex built the systems primarily to train neural networks and handle large-scale machine-learning workloads. All three rely on AMD EPYC processors and NVIDIA A100 accelerators connected through high-speed InfiniBand networking—hardware that Russian companies have found increasingly difficult to obtain in large quantities. One expert argued that restoring systems of this scale could prove far more difficult than simply repairing a damaged building. “It will not be possible to restore supercomputers of this level. And it is not even about the availability of money. The main problem is not even sanctions, but the shortage of chips and other components: there is a huge queue for them around the world. However, the costs of gray and black imports are also very high,” the specialist said. T-Invariant noted that Russia’s remaining major supercomputing capacity is concentrated around Moscow. Sberbank’s Christofari and Christofari Neo are located in Skolkovo, an area considered relatively well protected by air defenses, while MTS operates its GROM supercomputer in Lytkarino. Yandex also maintains other data centers in Mytishchi and Ivanteyevka in the Moscow region. artigo.texto: XBM USA and SiCAM Technologies Collaborate to Advance Next-Generation Silicon-Sulfur Battery Technology Collaboration pairs SiCAM’s low-cost silicon-carbon anode material with XBM’s sulfur cathode and cell technologies, to offer US battery OEMs an integrated silicon-sulfur (Si-S) battery platform. LOS ANGELES, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — XBM USA LLC (“XBM”) and SiCAM Technologies, Inc. (“SiCAM”) today announced a technology collaboration to develop a Silicon-Sulfur (Si-S) very high-energy-density battery materials platform by coupling SiCAM’s silicon-carbon (Si-C) anode material with XBM’s lithium-sulfur (Li-S) cathode materials and advanced cell technologies. Silicon-sulfur is amongst one of the most promising next-generation battery cathode and anode chemistry platforms, with substantially higher theoretical energy density than conventional li-ion batteries (LIBs). Silicon is the second-most-abundant element in the Earth’s crust, sulfur is a U.S. petroleum-refining byproduct, and XBM’s Li-S cathode is derived from lignin, an abundant U.S. paper pulping byproduct. Asia, predominantly China, currently controls ~80–95% of the global battery cell and materials supply chain. U.S. battery manufacturers are seeking better, lower-cost, domestically sourced chemistries that reduce reliance on foreign materials. This shift creates opportunities for U.S. OEMs to leapfrog legacy technologies. Jon Shan, Chief Technology Officer of XBM USA, said, Our near-term objective is to optimize our high-capacity Li-S cathode and SiCAM’s Si-C anode in a first-of-its-kind silicon-sulfur battery platform, initially targeting high-energy-density, lightweight eMobility battery applications such as eVTOLs and drones. SiCAM’s proprietary silicon anode material and process are unique amongst all other Si-C anode products made today. Most other Si-C anode material developers use silane (silicon) in a CVD process to make their Si-C anode products. SiCAM uses chlorosilane (TCS) silicon in a fluidized-bed chemical vapor deposition (FB-CVD) process. This novel approach creates a true bonded silicon-composite primary structure, helping to reduce the 300% silicon swelling problems experienced during battery charge and discharge cycles. On the cathode side, XBM’s high-capacity Li-sulfur cathode targets improved sulfur utilization, cycle life and cell-level energy density using abundant industrial byproducts, such as sulfur and lignin. Phillip Roberts, co-founder of SiCAM Technologies and XBM USA, said: This silicon-sulfur cell technology collaboration is the natural evolution of our company’s US centric “Sustainable Battery” vision avoiding longstanding battery chemistries that are mined, more expensive, and foreign sourced and controlled READ the latest Batteries News shaping the battery market XBM USA and SiCAM Technologies Collaborate to Advance Next-Generation Silicon-Sulfur Battery Technology, source

artigo.texto: Abengoa Major historical player, now restructured According to the latest IndexBox report on the global Parabolic Trough Collectors market, the market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals, more disciplined procurement behavior, and a more regionally diversified supply architecture. The global parabolic trough collectors (PTC) market is entering a phase of renewed strategic importance as energy systems prioritize dispatchable renewable capacity. Unlike photovoltaic systems, PTCs integrate cost-effective thermal energy storage, enabling electricity generation or industrial heat supply beyond daylight hours. This report analyzes the market from 2026 to 2035, covering complete collector assemblies, mirrors, receiver tubes, support structures, and tracking systems. The analysis identifies utility-scale CSP plants as the dominant end-use, while industrial process heat, district heating, desalination, and enhanced oil recovery offer diversification pathways. The competitive landscape features established engineering firms and specialized component manufacturers. Regional dynamics are shaped by solar resource quality, policy support, and local manufacturing capabilities. The forecast baseline assumes moderate policy continuity, declining technology costs, and growing recognition of long-duration storage value. Key risks include competition from PV-plus-battery systems, permitting delays, and supply chain concentration. The report provides a data-driven outlook for manufacturers, EPC contractors, investors, and policymakers navigating this evolving market. The baseline scenario for the parabolic trough collectors market from 2026 to 2035 anticipates moderate but steady expansion, with a compound annual growth rate of 4.2% in real terms. This outlook is anchored in the unique value proposition of PTCs: the ability to store thermal energy at scale, providing dispatchable power and heat that complements variable renewable sources. Demand growth will not replicate the subsidy-driven boom of the 2010s; instead, it will be driven by integrated energy projects, hybrid configurations, and industrial decarbonization mandates. Utility-scale CSP plants will remain the largest segment, but their share will gradually erode as industrial process heat and district heating applications gain traction. Technological improvements, including higher-temperature receivers and advanced molten salt systems, will enhance efficiency and lower levelized costs. Supply chain constraints for specialized components, such as evacuated receiver tubes, may temper growth in certain years. Geographically, the Middle East and Africa, along with Asia-Pacific, will account for the majority of new capacity additions, supported by national energy diversification plans. North America and Europe will see selective deployment, often linked to research or hybrid projects. The market index, with 2025 as the base year at 100, is projected to reach 151 by 2035, reflecting cumulative growth. This baseline assumes no major policy reversals and a gradual decline in capital costs, consistent with historical learning curves. Utility-scale CSP plants remain the primary end-use for parabolic trough collectors, leveraging the technology's proven ability to generate dispatchable electricity with integrated thermal energy storage. Currently, new CSP capacity is concentrated in the Middle East, North Africa, and parts of Asia, where strong solar resources and policy support align. Through 2035, demand will be driven by grid operators' need for flexible, firm capacity to balance high shares of photovoltaic and wind generation. The key demand-side indicators include national renewable energy targets, capacity auction schedules, and the levelized cost of storage. While the segment's absolute volume will grow, its share of the overall PTC market will decline as industrial and district heating applications expand. Hybridization with gas or PV will become more common, enhancing dispatchability and reducing risk. Major projects in countries like Morocco, Dubai, and Chile will anchor demand, but growth will be tempered by competition from alternative storage technologies. Current trend: Dominant but gradually declining share as other applications grow. Major trends: Integration of thermal energy storage for extended dispatchability, Hybridization with photovoltaic and gas turbines, Shift towards higher-temperature molten salt systems, Increasing project sizes in sunbelt regions, and Declining levelized cost of electricity. Representative participants: Abengoa, Sener, Acciona, Cobra Energía, and TSK Flagsol. Industrial process heat represents a rapidly emerging application for parabolic trough collectors, as manufacturers in sectors such as food processing, chemicals, and textiles seek to reduce carbon emissions from high-temperature steam generation. Currently, adoption is limited to pilot and demonstration projects, but declining costs and corporate sustainability commitments are accelerating deployment. Through 2035, demand will be driven by carbon pricing mechanisms, renewable heat incentives, and the need for reliable, on-site thermal energy. Key demand-side indicators include industrial energy prices, emissions regulations, and the availability of turnkey PTC solutions. Unlike CSP plants, industrial projects are smaller and modular, enabling faster deployment and lower capital risk. However, integration with existing steam systems and space constraints can pose challenges. The segment's share is expected to rise significantly, supported by growing interest from multinational corporations aiming for net-zero operations. Current trend: Fastest-growing segment, driven by decarbonization mandates. Major trends: Modular PTC systems for on-site steam generation, Corporate net-zero commitments driving adoption, Integration with existing industrial boilers, Government incentives for renewable heat, and Focus on cost reduction through standardized designs. artigo.texto: Operações de Data Center: Quando os riscos não se restringem à infraestrutura Na gestão de infraestrutura digital, uma interrupção de serviço pode resultar em perdas financeiras, de reputação e comerciais significativas. De acordo com a Análise Anual de Interrupções de Serviço de 2026 do Uptime Institute, 57% dos participantes da pesquisa relataram que sua interrupção de serviço mais recente custou mais de US$ 100.000; aproximadamente um quinto relatou perdas superiores a US$ 1 milhão. Notavelmente, o fator humano continua sendo uma das principais causas de incidentes graves. Os erros podem decorrer do não cumprimento de procedimentos, de procedimentos incompletos ou imprecisos, bem como de falhas que ocorrem durante a implantação e operação do sistema. Isso demonstra que investir em nova infraestrutura de hardware é apenas parte do problema do data center. Sem processos padronizados e disciplina operacional, o risco de interrupções ainda pode ocorrer. Da prata ao ouro: dois anos de padronização operacional A CMC Telecom obteve pela primeira vez a certificação Uptime TCOS Tier III Prata em 2024. Dois anos depois, na reavaliação de 2026, o Data Center Tan Thuan foi promovido para Ouro – o nível mais alto no sistema TCOS para sustentabilidade operacional. Simultaneamente, tornou-se um dos apenas 66 data centers em todo o mundo a alcançar o status Ouro do TCOS. Para atender aos requisitos do Uptime Institute, a CMC Telecom concentrou-se em aprimorar dois aspectos: processos operacionais e capacidades da equipe. Primeiramente, é necessária uma revisão abrangente de todo o sistema de processos, desde a revisão dos processos existentes e a adição de outros necessários até a otimização das etapas operacionais para identificar e mitigar riscos. Essa avaliação não deve se basear apenas na documentação, mas também incluir o conteúdo e a frequência dos treinamentos, entrevistas com a equipe e a aplicabilidade prática dos processos. Em seguida, a CMC Telecom concentrou-se em aprimorar as habilidades práticas de sua equipe técnica. Desenvolveram um programa de treinamento alinhado às necessidades da Uptime, com foco em cenários reais, desde monitoramento de turno e manutenção de rotina até resposta a emergências. Esse processo durou aproximadamente dois anos, abordando as deficiências da avaliação anterior e aprimorando gradualmente o sistema de gestão operacional. A certificação não é o objetivo final. Ao compartilhar suas impressões sobre a importância da certificação, o Sr. Le Minh Hieu, Diretor da Divisão de Data Centers da CMC Telecom, afirmou: “Para a CMC Telecom, a classificação TCOS Gold é uma base importante para afirmar nossa capacidade de gerenciar e operar Data Centers de acordo com os padrões internacionais.” Nossos clientes nos confiam a infraestrutura necessária para dar suporte às suas operações comerciais críticas. Portanto, o que eles precisam não é apenas um data center bem projetado, mas também recursos de gerenciamento de riscos, consistência operacional e a capacidade da equipe técnica de lidar com diversas situações. O valor do TCOS reside em ajudar a transformar normas técnicas em um sistema de gestão disciplinado, criando assim valor real e tranquilidade para os clientes.” Acompanhando diretamente a equipe técnica durante o processo de preparação e avaliação, o Sr. Pham Huy Hoang, Diretor Adjunto da Divisão de Data Center da CMC Telecom, compartilhou: “A classificação Gold TCOS Uptime é um reconhecimento dos esforços da equipe na padronização de processos, aprimoramento das capacidades de execução e manutenção da consistência nas operações.” "A certificação Ouro é apenas um marco. O próximo desafio é manter essa disciplina diariamente e fazer com que os requisitos da norma se tornem um hábito em todos os turnos, para todos os engenheiros e em todos os processos." A plataforma operacional para sistemas empresariais críticos. Este marco demonstra que as capacidades operacionais dos centros de dados do Vietname estão cada vez mais próximas dos padrões internacionais. Este marco também está alinhado com a estratégia abrangente de provedor de serviços da CMC Telecom, com um ecossistema de infraestrutura digital que conecta data centers, além de recursos em conectividade, serviços em nuvem, segurança cibernética e serviços gerenciados. À medida que bancos, instituições financeiras e corporações aceleram a transformação digital e a adoção de IA, os requisitos para data centers não se limitam mais à capacidade ou ao projeto da infraestrutura. A capacidade de operar de forma estável, controlar riscos e garantir a continuidade de sistemas críticos está se tornando um critério cada vez mais crucial na escolha de parceiros de infraestrutura pelas empresas. Para a CMC Telecom, a certificação Uptime TCOS Tier III Gold não é apenas uma certificação, mas um compromisso com a manutenção da disciplina operacional, comprovado na prática.
